method: Using the generalized Bethe ansatz framework, they analyze the constraints imposed by integrability on time-dependent interaction strengths.
result: They find that for static models with RG flow, the time-dependent strengths follow the RG trajectories; for RG-invariant strengths, they can be constant or time-dependent in specific constrained ways.
conclusion: The set of integrability-preserving time-dependent strengths is larger than the set corresponding to the RG protocol in non-Hermitian systems.

title: ShadowPath: Lookup-Private Credential Status Verification Over Authenticated State
authors: Patrick Herbke, Wolf Rieder, Christian Ren\'e Sechting, Huaning Yang, Sid Lamichhane, Philip Raschke, Axel K\"upper
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Verifiable credentials let holders present digitally signed claims without requiring the issuer to participate in every presentation. Revocation complicates this privacy model because a verifier must determine whether a credential remains valid. Existing status checks may expose recurring identifiers, registry positions, or request metadata. Such information can serve as stable handles to link separate presentations. ShadowPath moves the credential status lookup to the holder. For each presentation, the holder proves, in zero-knowledge, that the credential has not been revoked under the verifier-selected registry root. The verifier learns the status result but not observable metadata. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first evaluation of Verkle trees for credential revocation and compare them with sparse Merkle trees to assess their applicability in real world applications. The comparison tests whether reducing path depth with Verkle trees offsets the higher cost of KZG-based authentication. Across 30 desktop trials, median Groth16 proving took 371.6ms with sparse Merkle and 2.11s with Verkle. Verification took 3.70ms and 7.55ms, respectively. Groth16 Verkle proving took about 3s on both primary mobile devices. The results show that shorter authenticated paths do not necessarily yield cheaper zero-knowledge proofs. With fresh session randomness, verifier-visible status data do not reveal whether two presentations use the same credential under the stated assumption of session-value independence. This guarantee excludes issuer-verifier collusion and synchronization traffic.
tldr: ShadowPath proposes a holder-based credential revocation status verification scheme using zero-knowledge proofs and authenticated data structures like sparse Merkle and Verkle trees, evaluated for performance.
motivation: Credential revocation checks can leak metadata and link presentations, so a privacy-preserving method is needed.
method: The holder proves in zero-knowledge that a credential is not revoked under a verifier-selected registry root, comparing sparse Merkle trees and Verkle trees with KZG commitments.
result: Sparse Merkle trees yield faster Groth16 proving (371.6ms) than Verkle trees (2.11s) on desktop, while verification is slightly slower; mobile devices also show Verkle proving around 3s.
conclusion: Shorter authenticated paths do not necessarily reduce zero-knowledge proof cost, and the method protects against linking under certain assumptions.

title: The Generalized Random Access Problem For Linear Codes
authors: Anina Gruica, Antonio Petrillo, Ferdinando Zullo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random access is a central requirement in DNA-based storage systems: one would like to recover selected information symbols without sequencing the whole encoded object. A recent combinatorial model associates to a generator matrix [MATH] the random variable [MATH], measuring the number of sampled columns needed to recover the information vector [MATH]. We study the cardinality-based extremal and finite-geometric aspects of simultaneous multi-symbol recovery. For a nonempty set [MATH], let [MATH] denote the number of random column samples needed until all vectors [MATH], [MATH], lie in the span of the observed columns. This variable interpolates between the singleton random access problem and the full-recovery problem underlying coverage depth. For each [MATH], we introduce uniform worst-case and average parameters over all requested sets [MATH] with [MATH]. Using the known subset-counting formula for [MATH], we establish general upper and lower bounds for these parameters. In particular, the lower bounds are expressed through order statistics of the singleton recovery variables and specialize to the known singleton bounds when [MATH]. For systematic MDS encoders, we record an equivalent form of the known multi-symbol expectation formula and derive monotonicity and asymptotic consequences. For simplex encoders in arbitrary dimension, we obtain closed formulae in terms of Gaussian binomial coefficients; the full-recovery endpoint agrees with the known coverage-depth formula for simplex codes. Finally, in dimension three we study balanced quasi-arcs and compare their values with the simplex and MDS benchmarks.
tldr: This paper generalizes the random access problem for linear codes to simultaneous recovery of multiple information symbols, providing bounds and closed-form results for MDS and simplex encoders.
motivation: Random access is crucial for DNA-based storage systems to retrieve selected information without sequencing the entire encoded object. The study extends the singleton recovery problem to multi-symbol recovery, addressing both worst-case and average scenarios.
method: The authors define a random variable for the number of column samples needed to span a set of requested vectors, introduce uniform worst-case and average parameters over all requested sets, and use a known subset-counting formula to establish bounds. They specialize results for systematic MDS encoders and simplex encoders, leveraging Gaussian binomial coefficients, and study balanced quasi-arcs in dimension three.
result: General upper and lower bounds are expressed via order statistics of singleton recovery variables, with closed forms for simplex codes matching coverage-depth formulas. For MDS encoders, monotonicity and asymptotic consequences are derived, and comparisons with simplex and MDS benchmarks are made in dimension three.
conclusion: The paper advances the combinatorial understanding of multi-symbol recovery in linear codes, offering theoretical tools that may inform the design of efficient DNA-based storage systems.

title: Adaptive Error Budget Allocation For Fault-Tolerant Quantum Resource Estimation: A Metaheuristic Approach
authors: Tasnuva Farheen Asif Akhtab Ronggon
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System-level resource estimation is a key component of fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) toolchains. Its efficiency depends on how global error tolerance is allocated across logical operations, T-state distillation, and rotation synthesis to minimize physical resource overhead. The commonly used uniform-allocation strategy ignores circuit-specific structure and can overprovision inactive or less critical subsystems, leading to inflated space-time estimates. Prior work aims to address this limitation using supervised models trained on offline-generated datasets. However, this approach incurs additional data-generation costs and limits deployment flexibility. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose a training-free optimization framework that performs derivative-free search directly on the Azure Quantum Resource Estimator (AQRE), enabling instance-specific error budget allocation for previously unseen circuits without requiring offline training data. To evaluate robustness to optimizer choice, we instantiate the framework with two structurally distinct metaheuristics, simulated annealing and quantum particle swarm optimization. We evaluate our framework across 433 circuits spanning 2 to 91 qubits from 31 families in the MQT Bench suite. Across the benchmark suite, both methods reduce space-time cost by more than 33\% on average and agree within 1.34\% points, indicating that the gains are stable across different metaheuristic search strategies. Our analysis further finds that the optimization benefit is driven primarily by error-profile asymmetry rather than circuit scale, and the metric, Gini coefficient of optimized allocation, provides an interpretable diagnostic of expected improvement. Together, these results position adaptive error budget allocation as a system-software optimization layer for FTQC resource estimation pipeline.
tldr: This paper presents a training-free optimization framework for adaptive error budget allocation in fault-tolerant quantum resource estimation, using metaheuristics to reduce space-time cost by over 33% on average.
motivation: Uniform error allocation in FTQC resource estimation overprovisions resources, and supervised models require offline data generation. The goal is instance-specific allocation without training data.
method: They use derivative-free search (simulated annealing and quantum particle swarm optimization) directly on the Azure Quantum Resource Estimator, evaluated on 433 circuits from MQT Bench.
result: Both metaheuristics reduce space-time cost by more than 33% on average and agree within 1.34 percentage points; benefit is driven by error-profile asymmetry, and the Gini coefficient of optimized allocation predicts improvement.
conclusion: Adaptive error budget allocation is an effective system-software optimization layer for FTQC resource estimation pipelines.

title: Rural Commute Patterns
authors: Mohamed Khalafalla, Doreen Kobelo, Thobias Sando, Janeroza Matyeni
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transportation provides access to employment opportunities and essential services such as healthcare services, while urban areas have various transportation options, the situation differs in rural areas. Rural residents often have longer commute distances, limited access to public transit, and extended waiting times for public transportation if they exist, which can significantly impact their access to vital services and job opportunities. This study used data from the 2017 NHTS survey to examine the commuting patterns in rural areas by utilizing multinomial logistic regression to determine how various factors impact the choice of mode of transport in rural areas. Findings from this study revealed a higher dependency, 92.1%, on using personal vehicles when making trips in rural areas. Multinomial logistic regression results showed that socio-demographics, household, and trip characteristics affect the mode of transport used in a trip. Older adults, females, and individuals with higher education levels than high school graduates are less likely to use public transit when making trips. For household characteristics, the availability of vehicles in a household and households with higher income levels have lower probabilities of making a trip using public transit. Longer trip distances reduce the likelihood of a trip using active commuting modes such as walking and biking. These findings provide insights into understanding the transportation behaviors in rural areas and provide knowledge to be used in the planning and developing of transportation projects to promote equitable and accessible transportation in rural areas.
tldr: Studies rural commuting patterns using NHTS data and multinomial logistic regression, finding heavy reliance on personal vehicles.
motivation: Rural areas have limited transit options and longer commutes, affecting access to services and jobs.
method: Analyzed 2017 NHTS data with multinomial logistic regression to identify factors influencing transport mode choice.
result: 92.1% trips use personal vehicles; demographics, household vehicles, income, and trip distance affect mode choice.
conclusion: Provides insights for planning equitable and accessible rural transportation.

title: Dataflows And Computational Patterns For Hybrid Quantum-Classical Scientific Computing
authors: Ryan Landfield, Jordan J. Winetrout, Michael A. Sandoval
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical computing has emerged as the dominant paradigm for near-term quantum applications, yet hybrid workflows are typically described by individual algorithms rather than their underlying execution behavior. We introduce the Quantum Execution Locality Framework (QELF), a qualitative framework for characterizing hybrid quantum-classical workflows according to recurring dataflow structures and quantum execution locality, the extent to which computation remains resident on the Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) before host intervention or classical synchronization. From a representative cross-section of applications, QELF identifies five recurring computational patterns with distinct locality characteristics and discusses their implications for communication overhead, workflow organization, and future hybrid computing architectures. By providing a common vocabulary for reasoning about hybrid workloads, QELF establishes a foundation for future quantitative validation and the co-design of algorithms, runtime systems, and hybrid computing architectures.
tldr: Introduces a qualitative framework (QELF) to characterize hybrid quantum-classical workflows based on dataflow structures and quantum execution locality, identifying five recurring computational patterns.
motivation: Hybrid workflows are typically described individually rather than by underlying execution behavior, lacking a common vocabulary for analysis and co-design.
method: Proposes the Quantum Execution Locality Framework (QELF) and applies it to a representative cross-section of applications to identify recurring computational patterns.
result: Identifies five computational patterns with distinct quantum execution locality characteristics, and discusses implications for communication overhead, workflow organization, and future hybrid architectures.
conclusion: QELF provides a foundation for quantitative validation and the co-design of algorithms, runtime systems, and hybrid computing architectures.

title: Black-Box Coherence Matrix Eigen-Spectroscopy With Programmable Photonics
authors: Kevin Zelaya, Jonathan Friedman, Mohammad-Ali Miri
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The precise characterization of spatial optical coherence is fundamental to emerging applications in optical communications and computational imaging. However, extracting the full coherence matrix traditionally requires phase-sensitive interferometry, which is highly vulnerable to environmental noise and poses severe scalability challenges for integrated photonics. Here, we introduce an architecture-agnostic framework for analyzing and controlling partially coherent light on programmable photonic circuits. By leveraging the Schur-Horn theorem, our approach systematically diagonalizes the incident coherence matrix, relying solely on output intensity measurements and entirely circumventing the need for complex phase retrieval. We experimentally validate this black-box protocol on a low-depth, non-universal photonic integrated circuit, successfully reconstructing the hidden eigenvalues of mixed states generated from up to four mutually incoherent sources. Furthermore, we demonstrate active, in-situ statistical light control by introducing non-unitary amplitude modulation to significantly enhance interference visibility, exposing a fundamental physical trade-off between coherence enhancement and optical loss. Inherently resilient to hardware constraints and experimental noise, this scalable paradigm establishes a robust pathway for realizing ultra-compact, on-chip spatial coherence analyzers.
tldr: The paper presents a black-box, intensity-only method to characterize and control spatial coherence of light on programmable photonic circuits using the Schur-Horn theorem.
motivation: Traditional phase-sensitive interferometry for coherence characterization is noise-vulnerable and not scalable for integrated photonics, necessitating a more robust approach.
method: The method uses programmable photonic circuits to diagonalize the coherence matrix via the Schur-Horn theorem, relying solely on output intensity measurements, and is validated on a low-depth non-universal photonic circuit.
result: Experiments successfully reconstructed eigenvalues of mixed states from up to four mutually incoherent sources, and demonstrated active coherence control with amplitude modulation, revealing a trade-off between coherence enhancement and optical loss.
conclusion: This scalable, hardware-robust framework offers a promising path for ultra-compact, on-chip spatial coherence analyzers.

title: Measurement And Optimal Targeting Of A Hidden Scatterer In A Complex Environment Utilizing Fisher Information
authors: Nadav Shaibe, Jared Erb, Steven M. Anlage
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complex, non-Hermitian scattering system with a high degree of multiple scattering and interference is often treated as a black box, described simply by the relationship between a set of incoming and outgoing waves of a given frequency or energy. The scattering matrix S that describes the system is a non-unique, generally sub-unitary matrix that reveals very little about the microscopic processes that are responsible for the observed scattering. We form the Fisher information operator [MATH], a Hermitian matrix, utilizing a derivative of S with respect to the value of some varying parameter x of the system, associated with a localized perturbation, and experimentally demonstrate that the principal eigenvector of Fx can be used to quantitatively measure changes in the value of parameter x using only information from the scattering matrix. We propose a "discrete feedback loop" protocol enabled by the knowledge we gain from the Fisher information operator, that repeatedly determines the counter perturbation necessary to return a varying parameter to some fixed benchmark value. A further application of the Fisher information operator for energy focusing that utilizes the principal eigenvector excitation is demonstrated through compelling indirect evidence of targeting within a complex system. These methods are experimentally demonstrated to work even in the presence of time-reversal symmetry breaking due to absorption and/or loss of scattering reciprocity.
tldr: This paper demonstrates using the Fisher information operator derived from scattering matrix derivatives to measure and target hidden scatterers in complex environments.
motivation: To extract information about microscopic processes in complex scattering systems without full characterization, and to enable precise control of wave propagation.
method: They construct the Fisher information operator from the derivative of the scattering matrix with respect to a parameter, and use its principal eigenvector for parameter measurement and a discrete feedback loop for targeting.
result: Experimental demonstrations show the principal eigenvector quantitatively measures parameter changes and enables energy focusing and targeting, even with time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The Fisher information operator is a powerful tool for sensing and control in complex scattering media, with potential applications in wave-based imaging and communication.

title: Efficient Classical Simulation Of Weakly Interacting Fermion Dynamics
authors: Chu Zhao, Iman Marvian, Yu Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the task of simulating the real-time dynamics of weakly interacting fermionic systems. In particular, we focus on computing the expectation value of a local observable [MATH] at time [MATH]. By analyzing the convergence of the perturbative expansion in the interaction strength [MATH] for the Heisenberg-picture observable, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm for estimating this expectation value in the weakly interacting regime [MATH], when the Hamiltonian is geometrically local on a [MATH]-dimensional lattice. Importantly, this condition is independent of the system size. If the goal is instead to approximate the time-evolved observable in normalized Frobenius norm, we extend the convergence regime to [MATH] with quasi-polynomial runtime. When the non-interacting part exhibits Anderson localization, our polynomial-time algorithm can be extended up to [MATH], modulo polylogarithmic factors. Our algorithm brings together ideas from continuous-time QMC, diagrammatic QMC, and Majorana Propagation, but with a new Heisenberg-picture operator-growth analysis that makes the sampling complexity rigorously controllable. This leads to provably efficient classical algorithms in regimes where the interaction is weak enough that the sampling variance remains bounded independently of system size. Together, these results identify broad regimes in which weak interactions, locality, and localization can be leveraged to make real-time fermionic dynamics classically tractable.
tldr: This paper presents polynomial-time classical algorithms for simulating real-time dynamics of weakly interacting fermionic systems under certain conditions.
motivation: To determine when quantum many-body dynamics can be efficiently simulated classically, leveraging weak interactions and locality.
method: Uses perturbative expansions in interaction strength, combining ideas from continuous-time QMC, diagrammatic QMC, and Majorana propagation, with rigorous control of sampling complexity.
result: Achieves polynomial-time algorithms for geometrically local Hamiltonians in weakly interacting regime, and extends to Anderson localization.
conclusion: Identifies regimes where weak interactions, locality, and localization make real-time fermionic dynamics classically tractable.

title: Renormalization Group Ontology In Quantum Foundations: A Non-interacting Spin-0 Toy Model
authors: Gary Kapilevich
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A realist, anti-psi interpretation of quantum field theory is introduced, based on an expanded ontology that was inspired by the renormalization group. A goal will be to work with a classical non-interacting scalar field "toy model" in the canonical ensemble and show that an observer in this expanded ontology, under certain limiting conditions, will see a QFT. The inverse renormalization group (IRG) will be key in both interpreting this expanded ontology and furnishing novel examples of QFTs. This will lead to a definition of Planck's constant that flows as we head towards a fixed point, is expressed in terms of a temperature, and depends on the observer being studied in this expanded ontology. Our hope is that this approach will lead both to insights into quantum foundations and to prescriptions for developing new QFTs.
tldr: Proposes a realist interpretation of quantum field theory using renormalization group ontology, illustrated with a non-interacting scalar field toy model.
motivation: To provide a new perspective on quantum foundations and potentially derive new QFTs.
method: Uses a classical non-interacting scalar field in the canonical ensemble and the inverse renormalization group to show that an observer sees a QFT under limiting conditions.
result: Defines Planck's constant as a quantity that flows with temperature and depends on the observer in the expanded ontology.
conclusion: The approach may offer insights into quantum foundations and lead to prescriptions for developing new QFTs.

title: Which Pulse Maximizes Resonant Nonlinear Conversion?
authors: Alex Krasnok
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At fixed pulse energy, which drive waveform extracts the most [MATH]th-order nonlinear conversion from a resonator ([MATH] for second harmonic)? A short pulse couples poorly to a narrow resonance, a long one dilutes its energy, and no linear rule fixes the compromise. We solve the problem exactly for a single mode of amplitude decay rate [MATH]. Eliminating the drive turns fixed incident energy into a constraint on the stored field alone, and the optimization becomes a sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality whose extremal is the ground-state soliton of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. The optimal stored field is [MATH], sustained by an asymmetric input that rises as [MATH] and falls as [MATH]; the largest converted energy follows in closed form. A rising exponential, the time-reversal recipe, retains at most [MATH] of the bound at [MATH] and [MATH] at large [MATH]; a two-rate pulse retains above [MATH]. Critical coupling generalizes to [MATH]-fold overcoupling, with optimal input coupling [MATH] times the intrinsic loss rate. The bound applies from microrings to superconducting circuits and caps the per-pulse brightness of broadband photon-pair sources.
tldr: The paper derives the optimal pulse shape for maximizing nonlinear conversion in a resonator using a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality and soliton solutions.
motivation: To determine the drive waveform that extracts the most nth-order nonlinear conversion from a resonator at fixed pulse energy, balancing pulse duration and resonance coupling.
method: Reformulates the optimization as a constraint on the stored field, yielding a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality whose extremal is a soliton of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation; derives the optimal input shape and conversion bound.
result: The optimal stored field is a soliton, sustained by an asymmetric input (rising and falling exponentials), and the maximum converted energy is given in closed form; critical coupling generalizes to n-fold overcoupling.
conclusion: The derived universal bound applies to various systems like microrings and superconducting circuits, and caps the per-pulse brightness of broadband photon-pair sources.

title: Geometry-Encoded Multireceiver Fluorometry Enables Full-Range Nonlinear Quantification Under The Inner Filter Effect
authors: Shuiyi Tan, Nai-Quan Zhu, Olivier J. F. Martin, Yuchao Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inner filter effect (IFE) transforms the nominally linear fluorescence-concentration relationship into a geometry-dependent and often nonmonotonic response, resulting in reduced sensitivity, concentration ambiguity, and inaccurate underestimation at high optical densities. Here, we introduce a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that does not eliminate or correct the IFE, but instead harnesses the spatial fluorescence attenuation induced by IFE as an additional quantitative encoding dimension. Fluorescence generated along the excitation axis is integrated over independently positioned receiver windows, and concentration is recovered by nonlinear optimization of the joint fluorescent intensity vector. Tryptophan was selected as a biomedically relevant model fluorophore to validate the proposed strategy. Single-window calibration exhibited vanishing-gradient boundary and two-valued concentration inversions, whereas two spatially separated receiver windows restored global identifiability across the full concentration range. Screening of 35 two-receiver geometries identified the minimum-uncertainty configuration, achieving an average 95% error half-width of mean E_95= 0.884 mg/L, and the maximum-sensitivity configuration, reaching a noise-normalized response sensitivity of mean S_N=3.832 a.u./(mg/L). By converting spatial attenuation into a multidimensional concentration coordinate, this approach extends quantitative fluorescence analysis without dilution, a separate absorbance measurement, or piecewise calibration and provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence metrology even under strong IFE conditions.
tldr: Introduces a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that exploits the inner filter effect for full-range concentration quantification without dilution.
motivation: The inner filter effect leads to nonlinearity and ambiguity in fluorescence-based quantification, causing reduced sensitivity and inaccurate measurements, while existing methods require corrections or dilution.
method: Uses multiple receiver windows at different positions along the excitation axis to capture fluorescence signals attenuated by the inner filter effect, and recovers concentration via nonlinear optimization of the joint intensity vector, screening geometries for optimal configurations.
result: Two receiver windows restore global identifiability across the full concentration range, achieving low error (E_95=0.884 mg/L) and high sensitivity (S_N=3.832 a.u./(mg/L)) for tryptophan.
conclusion: This approach provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence quantification even under strong inner filter effect, avoiding dilution or separate absorbance measurements.

title: Exact Partition Function Of Arithmetic Ising Model
authors: Anu Dhochak, Ken Kikuchi, Shrinit Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a compact formula for the exact partition function of the [MATH]-dimensional arithmetic Ising model (AIM). For a [MATH] system, we express it analytically using the [MATH]-Hurwitz-Lerch zeta function and derive explicit forms for the free energy and entropy. Additionally, we find that the entropy increases at high temperatures, supporting the presence of entropic order.
tldr: This paper derives the exact partition function of the arithmetic Ising model using the Hurwitz-Lerch zeta function and analyzes its entropy, finding entropic order at high temperatures.
motivation: To obtain an exact analytical solution for the arithmetic Ising model, which may exhibit novel thermodynamic behavior and entropic ordering.
method: The authors express the partition function analytically using the Hurwitz-Lerch zeta function and derive explicit forms for free energy and entropy from it.
result: They find that entropy increases at high temperatures, supporting the presence of entropic order.
conclusion: The exact solution provides insights into the phase structure and entropic ordering of the arithmetic Ising model.

title: Moore--Read Construction And Explicit Monodromies Of Laughlin States On Riemann Surfaces
authors: Kiyoon Eum
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the Moore--Read construction of the [MATH] Laughlin states on compact Riemann surfaces, deriving their conformal blocks from [MATH] Chern--Simons theory through the CS/WZW correspondence. We compute their explicit monodromies under quasi-hole transport and Aharonov--Bohm flux insertion, and conjecture that these coincide with the corresponding adiabatic holonomies. Under this identification, we recover classical results on Laughlin states including the flux-averaged Hall conductance [MATH] via a vector bundle of Laughlin states over [MATH]. We also relate our construction to the recently developed algebro-geometric approach to higher genus Laughlin states.
tldr: This paper revisits the Moore–Read construction of Laughlin states on Riemann surfaces, deriving conformal blocks from Chern–Simons theory and computing explicit monodromies.
motivation: To provide explicit monodromies for Laughlin states under quasi-hole transport and flux insertion, and relate them to adiabatic holonomies and Hall conductance.
method: Uses CS/WZW correspondence and conformal field theory to construct Laughlin states, and computes monodromies via explicit calculations.
result: Recovers classical results on Laughlin states, including flux-averaged Hall conductance, and relates to algebro-geometric approaches.
conclusion: The construction provides a rigorous framework for Laughlin states on higher genus surfaces.

title: Shift Or Curtail? How Much Data-center Flexibility Is Worth Depends On The Host Power Grid
authors: Saroj Khanal, Geon Roh, Boyu Yao, Abraham Silverman, Dennice Gayme, Charalambos Konstantinou, Jip Kim, Yury Dvorkin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-center growth risks overbuilding power grid infrastructure and stranding capital. Flexible data-center operation can defer infrastructure investments, but its value depends on the flexibility mechanism and the host power grid characteristics. We classify data-center load as firm, flexible or interruptible, and embed them in capacity expansion applied to market-organized, fossil-heavy PJM and carbon-capped, centrally coordinated Korea. In PJM, the flexibility value is spatial: shifting workloads between zones reduces system cost by 6% in 2028 and 19% in 2038, avoiding 4.4 GW and 8.9 GW of gas and nuclear generation. In Korea, it is temporal: shifting load into midday solar hours makes 0.5 GW of additional solar worth building in 2028 and avoids 1.2 GW of gas and 0.3 GW of batteries in 2038. In both, realistic event-shape limits diminish the value of curtailment. The results show that flexibility procurement and its value are driven by grid characteristics and policy objectives.
tldr: This paper analyzes the value of data-center load flexibility in deferring power grid investments, showing that the value depends on grid characteristics and flexibility mechanisms.
motivation: Data-center growth may lead to overbuilding grid infrastructure; flexible operation could defer investments, but its value is not well quantified.
method: The authors embed firm, flexible, and interruptible data-center loads into a capacity expansion model applied to PJM (market-based, fossil-heavy) and Korea (centrally coordinated, carbon-capped), comparing spatial and temporal flexibility.
result: In PJM, spatial shifting between zones reduces system cost by 6% (2028) and 19% (2038), avoiding significant generation; in Korea, temporal shifting into solar hours enables additional solar and avoids gas and batteries; realistic event-shape limits reduce curtailment value.
conclusion: The value of data-center flexibility is highly context-dependent, driven by grid characteristics and policy objectives, and should be considered in grid planning.

title: Assembly Theory And The Smallest Grammar Problem
authors: Wawrzyniec Bieniawski
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assembly theory (AT) quantifies complexity through the assembly index (ASI) -- a metric proven equivalent to the size of the smallest straight-line program (SLP). While this equivalence links AT to data compression -- a field shaped by decades of research -- the practical efficacy of specific algorithms as ASI approximators remains largely unexplored. This study provides an empirical evaluation of eight compression algorithms, spanning grammar-based and dictionary schemes (CAs) across a dataset of 408 strings -- comprising 368 synthetic strings (including max-complexity strings and strings with varying levels of symbol distribution balance, quantified by Shannon entropy) and 40 natural biological sequences (genomic and proteomic). We introduce Re-Pair T-NDR, a branch-and-bound tie-resolving variant of Re-Pair, providing a tighter upper bound on the ASI than the other CAs researched in this study. Increasing alphabet size extends the regime in which CAs closely track the ASI, delaying a ``divergence point'', where a CA deviates from the optimal assembly path. The results establish compression algorithms as practical tools for ASI estimation.
tldr: This paper empirically evaluates eight compression algorithms as estimators of the assembly index (ASI), introduces a new Re-Pair variant, and shows that compression algorithms can practically approximate the assembly index.
motivation: Assembly theory quantifies complexity via the assembly index, which is equivalent to the smallest grammar problem, but the practical performance of compression algorithms as ASI approximators had not been systematically evaluated.
method: The authors test eight grammar-based and dictionary compression algorithms on 408 strings (synthetic and biological), and introduce Re-Pair T-NDR, a branch-and-bound tie-resolving variant of Re-Pair.
result: Re-Pair T-NDR yields a tighter upper bound on the ASI than the other algorithms; increasing alphabet size delays the divergence point where a compression algorithm deviates from the optimal assembly path.
conclusion: Compression algorithms are practical tools for ASI estimation, with Re-Pair T-NDR providing the best performance among the tested methods.

title: The Second Edge Theorem: The Asymptotic Collapse Of Sample-Dependent Information Geometry To The Canonical Flat Canvas Of Conventional Statistics In Large Sample Limits
authors: Bing Cheng, Yi-Shuai Niu, Howell Tong, Shing-Tung Yau
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes the global proof of the Second Edge Theorem: as sample size tends to infinity, sample-dependent information-geometric manifolds---formed by the parameter space, sample-scaled Fisher metric, and dual alpha-connections---undergo metric-topological collapse onto the flat tangent space of Conventional Statistics at the true parameter. We first prove a universal tensor valence scaling law, under which tensor fields of valence one through four degenerate at rates determined by sample size. Score fluctuations stabilize, the Fisher metric freezes to its true-parameter value, affine connections dissolve, and Riemann curvature is annihilated. We then bridge geometric collapse with statistical decision theory, showing that Cheeger--Gromov flattening and Le Cam risk condensation are dual projections of the same asymptotic phase transition. A Fisher-compatible Ehresmann connection extends these results to over-parameterized and singular models, yielding horizontal leaf-space collapse and uniform local asymptotic normality. Unifying the First and Second Edge Theorems yields a nested dual-edge hierarchy: Conventional Statistics is the boundary of Information Geometry, which is itself the boundary of Statistical Mechanics and Geometry. Thus, Conventional Statistics is not a heuristic approximation but the unique zero-curvature thermodynamic attractor of regular parametric information manifolds. This redefines modern statistics as a dynamic non-equilibrium field theory of finite-sample fluctuations, phase transitions, and gauge-invariant interactions.
tldr: This paper proves the Second Edge Theorem, showing that sample-dependent information-geometric manifolds collapse to the flat geometry of conventional statistics in large sample limits, bridging information geometry, statistics, and thermodynamics.
motivation: To establish a rigorous global proof of the asymptotic collapse of information geometry to classical statistics and to explore the hierarchical relationship between these fields.
method: The paper uses tensor valence scaling laws, Cheeger-Gromov flattening, Le Cam risk condensation, and a Fisher-compatible Ehresmann connection to analyze the degeneracy of tensor fields and manifold geometry as sample size grows.
result: As sample size tends to infinity, the Fisher metric freezes, affine connections dissolve, and Riemann curvature vanishes, leading to metric-topological collapse and uniform local asymptotic normality.
conclusion: Conventional statistics is the unique zero-curvature thermodynamic attractor of information manifolds, redefining statistics as a non-equilibrium field theory.

title: Information Geometry (ig) Lives At Edge Or Boundary Of Smg (statistically Meaningful Geometry): - The First Edge Theorem And Applications
authors: Bing Cheng, Yi-Shuai Niu, Howell Tong, Shing-Tung Yau
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistically Meaningful Geometry (SMG) is a differential-geometric and information-theoretic framework that lifts over-parameterized models into infinite-dimensional non-parametric Orlicz statistical fiber bundles with an Ehresmann connection, decoupling unobservable vertical gauge noise from horizontal statistically verifiable directions. We prove the First Edge Theorem: Amari's information geometry (IG) and conventional statistics (CS) are not autonomous statistical universes but degenerate boundary layers of the larger gauge-active SMG space. Taking the structural identifiability radius [MATH] breaks gauge symmetry, collapses vertical fibers, and forces the total space onto the IG manifold; subsequent local asymptotic normality as [MATH] flattens the remaining curvature, yielding \[ . \] The same fiber-bundle machinery transforms model non-identifiability from a singular collapse into a structured gauge space. Applications include resolving the deep-learning generalization paradox, constructing gauge-invariant gradient descent and holonomy-matched preference alignment for generative AI, and solving weak identification in structural econometrics via intrinsic horizontal geodesic search.
tldr: This paper introduces a new framework called Statistically Meaningful Geometry (SMG) that unifies information geometry and conventional statistics as boundary layers, and applies it to machine learning and econometrics.
motivation: To resolve issues like model identifiability and deep learning generalization by providing a more general geometric framework.
method: The paper constructs infinite-dimensional non-parametric Orlicz statistical fiber bundles with an Ehresmann connection and proves the First Edge Theorem.
result: It shows that Amari's information geometry and conventional statistics are degenerate cases of the larger SMG space, and demonstrates applications in deep learning and econometrics.
conclusion: The SMG framework offers a unified perspective and practical tools for addressing weak identifiability and improving generalization.

title: Minimum Attaining Operators On Reducing Subspaces: Spectral Structure And Density
authors: Golla Ramesh Puspendu Nag
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we introduce and investigate a new subclass [MATH] of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space [MATH]. This class contains the absolutely minimum attaining operators and is properly contained in the class of minimum attaining operators. We establish several structural and spectral characterizations of operators in [MATH]. In particular, we characterize positive operators in [MATH] in terms of their spectral representations. We prove that [MATH] is dense in [MATH] in the operator norm and, moreover, that the operators in [MATH] having a nontrivial invariant half-space are also dense in [MATH] in the operator norm. We further obtain a representation theorem for normal operators in [MATH] and establish additional structural properties of this class.
tldr: This paper introduces a new subclass of minimum attaining operators on Hilbert spaces and studies its spectral structure and density properties.
motivation: To refine the understanding of minimum attaining operators by introducing a more constrained subclass and proving structural and spectral characterizations.
method: The authors use functional analysis and operator theory, including spectral representations for positive operators and density arguments in the operator norm.
result: They establish characterizations for positive and normal operators in the new class, prove density in the operator norm, and show density of operators with nontrivial invariant half-spaces.
conclusion: The new subclass has advantageous properties that provide deeper insight into minimum attaining operators, though its relevance to the user's research directions is minimal.

title: Existence Of Periodic Solutions For Hamiltonian Inclusion Systems Using Clarke Duality
authors: Fernando D. Mazzone Stefania M. Demaria
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of periodic solutions for Hamiltonian differential inclusions under growth conditions involving a G-function.
tldr: 该论文证明了在涉及G-函数的增长条件下，哈密顿包含系统周期解的存在性。
motivation: 研究哈密顿包含系统的动力学行为，这些系统在工程和物理中具有广泛的应用，但周期解的存在性尚未完全解决。
method: 使用Clarke对偶方法，结合G-函数给出的增长条件，建立周期解存在的充分条件。
result: 在给定的增长条件下，证明了哈密顿包含系统存在非平凡的周期解。
conclusion: 该结果为哈密顿包含系统的周期解理论提供了新的数学保证，但与本用户的研究方向无关。

title: A High-Order Rank-Adaptive Implicit Algorithm For Solving High Dimensional Diffusion Equations Using The Hierarchical Tucker Decomposition
authors: Paolo Bosques-Paulet
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a high-order rank-adaptive implicit integrator for the tensor solution of high-dimensional diffusion equations. We extend the 3D version of this method from the Tucker decomposition to higher dimensions using the hierarchical Tucker (HT) decomposition, since the storage complexity for the Tucker decomposition increases exponentially with the number of dimensions [MATH]. The HT format avoids this issue by decomposing the solution according to a binary tree consisting of bases for each dimension and core tensors which connect the bases. Spectral methods are considered for spatial discretization, and diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta methods are considered for time discretization. At each stage of the Runge-Kutta method, the bases computed at the previous stages are augmented to predict the upcoming basis and construct projection subspaces. By projecting onto these enriched subspaces, the bases and cores can be updated in a sequential manner going up the tree from leaf-to-root. Unlike the 3D Tucker method which has a single core tensor, the HT method also updates the intermediate core tensors. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method observes high-order accuracy, and test how well the integrator captures the solution rank for various sets of time-dependent diffusion coefficients.
tldr: This paper proposes a high-order rank-adaptive implicit integrator for high-dimensional diffusion equations using hierarchical Tucker decomposition, but it is unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To efficiently solve high-dimensional diffusion problems by extending a 3D Tucker decomposition method to higher dimensions using hierarchical Tucker decomposition to avoid exponential storage growth.
method: The method combines spectral spatial discretization with diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta time stepping, and updates hierarchical Tucker bases and cores sequentially from leaf to root using enriched projection subspaces.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy and good rank adaptation for various time-dependent diffusion coefficients.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm effectively handles high-dimensional diffusion equations, but its scope is purely numerical analysis with no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Implicit-adjoint Finite-volume Topology Optimization Of Two-dimensional Conjugate Heat Transfer
authors: Sam Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing compact, high-efficiency thermal architectures requires resolving the competing demands of solid conduction, fluid convection, and flow resistance within highly constrained physical envelopes. Density-based topology optimization provides a systematic framework for synthesizing these coupled layouts, yet the reproducibility and numerical stability of the resulting designs depend critically on the underlying discrete solvers and adjoint sensitivity mechanics. In this work, we present a transparent, self-contained two-dimensional finite-volume formulation on a staggered Marker-and-Cell grid for conjugate heat transfer governed by design-dependent energy transport coupled to Stokes--Brinkman or Darcy flow at fixed solid volume. To prevent spurious artificial thermal sources in porous, weakly compressible Brinkman domains, the discrete advection operator is constructed to satisfy the identity [MATH] cellwise, ensuring that uniform temperature fields remain exact discrete nullspaces even under inexact continuity satisfaction. Reverse-mode derivatives are evaluated via the implicit function theorem rather than unrolled iterative loops, yielding exact discrete adjoints with bounded memory requirements. The discrete operators are systematically validated through the method of manufactured solutions and directional Taylor remainder tests. Four representative thermofluid design benchmarks are optimized using a projected-gradient scheme with [MATH]-continuation, wherein candidate iterates are accepted and published only upon satisfying rigorous, predeclared gates on residual convergence, mass conservation, volume feasibility, and numerical finiteness. The resulting formulation provides an inspectable, deterministic reference stack for verifiable conjugate thermofluidic topology optimization.
tldr: This paper presents a finite-volume topology optimization method for conjugate heat transfer using implicit adjoint sensitivity, with a focus on numerical stability and reproducibility.
motivation: To address the need for transparent and stable numerical frameworks for optimizing thermal architectures that involve coupled solid conduction, fluid convection, and flow resistance.
method: The method uses a staggered Marker-and-Cell grid, a discrete advection operator that satisfies exact nullspace conditions, and reverse-mode derivatives via the implicit function theorem to compute exact discrete adjoints with bounded memory.
result: The formulation is validated through method of manufactured solutions and directional Taylor tests, and applied to four thermofluid design benchmarks with rigorous convergence and feasibility gates.
conclusion: The proposed approach provides an inspectable, deterministic reference stack for verifiable conjugate thermofluidic topology optimization.

title: Equidistribution And Thermodynamics At Infinity
authors: Godofredo Iommi, Felipe Riquelme, An\'ibal Velozo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove level-2 large deviation upper bounds for potentials on countable Markov shifts and for suspension semi-flows over countable Markov shifts. For strongly positive recurrent potentials, we establish equidistribution of weighted empirical measures toward the corresponding equilibrium state. We then apply these results to interval maps, obtaining, in particular, equidistribution and large-deviation estimates for measures supported on boundary points. For the Gauss map, this yields equidistribution results on rational numbers, including a theorem of David and Shapira.
tldr: The paper proves large deviation upper bounds and equidistribution results for countable Markov shifts and suspension flows, with applications to interval maps and the Gauss map.
motivation: To understand asymptotic behavior of dynamical systems, particularly large deviations and equidistribution of measures, with applications to number theory.
method: Uses thermodynamic formalism for countable Markov shifts, proving level-2 large deviation upper bounds and establishing equidistribution of weighted empirical measures.
result: Establishes large deviation and equidistribution results for interval maps and specifically for the Gauss map on rational numbers, recovering a theorem of David and Shapira.
conclusion: The results provide a general framework for studying large deviations and equidistribution in non-compact dynamical systems.

title: Beyond Linear Subspaces: Nonlinear Moment Matching Meets Quadratic Manifolds
authors: Serkan Gugercin Reetish Padhi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic manifold-based model order reduction offers a viable pathway to circumvent the limitations of linear subspaces for linear control systems characterized by slow Kolmogorov [MATH]-width decay. However, a system-theoretic framework for constructing such quadratic approximations remains absent from the literature. This paper presents a system-agnostic, optimization-free framework for the direct construction of quadratic projection matrices. We prove that the synthesized reduced-order model matches the nonlinear moments of the full-order system and preserves its exact center manifold mapping, thereby ensuring asymptotic tracking of steady-state outputs under specific input classes. Numerical results on transport-dominated benchmark problems, namely, the one-dimensional damped wave and advection equations, show that the proposed framework achieves high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction within a significantly reduced-dimensional state space, yielding substantial online computational savings.
tldr: This paper introduces a system-agnostic framework for constructing quadratic projection matrices in model order reduction, enabling nonlinear moment matching and exact center manifold preservation for linear control systems with slow Kolmogorov n-width decay.
motivation: Linear subspace approximations fail for systems with slowly decaying Kolmogorov n-width, motivating the need for nonlinear (quadratic) manifolds. Existing approaches lack a rigorous system-theoretic framework.
method: The authors propose an optimization-free, system-agnostic method to directly construct quadratic projection matrices, proving that the reduced model matches nonlinear moments and preserves the exact center manifold mapping.
result: Numerical tests on transport-dominated benchmarks (1D damped wave and advection equations) show high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction in significantly reduced dimensions, yielding substantial online computational savings.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled quadratic manifold approach for model reduction, achieving accuracy and efficiency in challenging problems where linear subspaces fail.

title: The Normal Procrustes Problem: A Riemannian Optimization Approach
authors: Kyle Bierly
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For given [MATH] data matrices [MATH], we investigate the Normal Procrustes Problem---the least squares optimization problem that aims to minimize [MATH], where [MATH] is constrained to be a normal [MATH] matrix. As far as the author of this article is aware, no other method that attempts to solve the Normal Procrustes Problem exists in the literature; we thus propose what is, to our knowledge, the first such method. We, furthermore, adapt our approach to address the Real Normal Procrustes Problem, where [MATH] must be real. In our treatment of these problems, we first reduce our complex and real objective functions to be purely optimizable over the Riemannian manifolds of the unitary and real orthogonal matrices, respectively. This reduction enables us to apply techniques in Riemannian manifold optimization to approximate solutions to both. The Closest Normal Matrix and Real Closest Normal Matrix Problems are both special cases of their respective Procrustes Problems and have been previously studied in the literature. Our approach thus recovers a novel Riemannian optimization method for approximating solutions to both these problems. We further numerically test the performance of our method across all such problems (including against previously developed algorithms on the Closest Normal Matrix Problems) and obtain competitive residuals and favorable scaling in wall-clock time.
tldr: This paper presents the first method to solve the Normal Procrustes Problem using Riemannian optimization on unitary and orthogonal manifolds.
motivation: No prior method exists for the Normal Procrustes Problem, so the author proposes a novel approach.
method: The complex and real objective functions are reduced to optimizations over unitary and orthogonal manifolds, then solved with Riemannian optimization techniques.
result: The method yields competitive residuals and favorable scaling in wall-clock time compared to existing algorithms for the closest normal matrix problems.
conclusion: The Riemannian optimization approach effectively solves the Normal Procrustes Problem and generalizes to the real case and closest normal matrix problems.

title: An Adaptive And Conservative Low-rank Imex Solver For The Hybrid Ion Vlasov-Fokker-Planck And Fluid Electron System
authors: Joseph Nakao, Dylan T. Jacobs, William Taitano
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a macroscopically conservative, rank-adaptive method for solving a hybrid Vlasov-Fokker-Planck (VFP) equation in which the ions are treated kinetically, and the electrons are treated as a fluid. Solving this system poses several coupled computational challenges: the curse of dimensionality, conservation of macroscopic quantities, stiffness arising from the multiscale nature of the model, and structure preservation. To address these challenges, we combine several established methods, each targeting a specific difficulty, into a unified framework for solving this nonlinear system. Specifically, we employ the recent Reduced Augmentation Implicit Low-rank (RAIL) method for rank adaptivity in velocity space to combat the curse of dimensionality, high-order implicit-explicit time stepping to handle the multiscale stiffness, and the Local Macroscopic Conservative (LoMaC) procedure for conservative truncation of the solution. The RAIL and LoMaC methods are extended from Cartesian to cylindrical coordinates. The resulting framework accommodates implicit rank-adaptive time integration while remaining conservative and leveraging structure-preserving discretizations. We verify the scheme on a suite of test problems and simulate a standing shock to demonstrate the importance of conserving the macroscopic quantities.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical solver for a hybrid Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system combining low-rank, implicit-explicit time stepping, and conservative truncation methods.
motivation: The hybrid kinetic-fluid model poses coupled computational challenges including high dimensionality, stiffness, and the need for conservation and structure preservation.
method: The framework integrates the Reduced Augmentation Implicit Low-rank (RAIL) method for rank adaptivity, high-order implicit-explicit time stepping, and the Local Macroscopic Conservative (LoMaC) procedure, extended to cylindrical coordinates.
result: The scheme is verified on test problems and a standing shock simulation, demonstrating the importance of conserving macroscopic quantities.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively addresses the numerical challenges of the hybrid Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system while maintaining conservation and structure preservation.

title: Tau-Rho Equality And Other Dependence Measures Of A Subclass Of Factorizable Copulas
authors: Noppawit Yanpaisan, Tippawan Santiwipanont, Matthias Scherer, Songkiat Sumetkijakan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho, two widely used dependence measures in statistics and risk management, are often treated as interchangeable, yet can disagree sharply: Schreyer et al.~(2017) established the exact region of attainable [MATH] pairs. We study the complementary question of equality, namely, identifying nontrivial families of copulas [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. We prove that this equality holds for every factorizable copula of the form [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are piecewise linear monotonic surjections (PLMS). For these PLMS-generated copulas, we study further dependence measures, including Chatterjee's rank correlation coefficient and tail dependence coefficients, revealing some useful algebraic formulas and unexpected phenomena. In particular, Chatterjee's coefficient can exhibit extreme asymmetry.
tldr: This paper studies conditions for equality of Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho in a subclass of factorizable copulas and analyzes additional dependence measures.
motivation: To complement the known region of attainable (tau, rho) pairs by characterizing copulas where these measures coincide.
method: They examine factorizable copulas generated by piecewise linear monotonic surjections and derive algebraic formulas for dependence measures.
result: They prove equality holds for these copulas and reveal unexpected asymmetry in Chatterjee's rank correlation coefficient.
conclusion: The work extends understanding of dependence measures for specific copula families, though the relevance to quantum information is negligible.

title: Nonexistence Of Frame Measures For Separated Uniform Consecutive-Digit Bernoulli Convolutions
authors: Wei-Jie Wang Xiao-Ye Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the existence problem of frame measures for uniform consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolutions under the separated scaling condition. Given parameters [MATH] and [MATH], we prove that if [MATH] for some integers [MATH] and [MATH], with [MATH], then the associated [MATH]-Bernoulli convolution [MATH] admits no frame measure. The proof introduces a new cyclic mask-quotient obstruction adapted to the multi-character structure of the consecutive-digit framework.
tldr: This paper proves that under a separated scaling condition, uniform consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolutions admit no frame measures, using a new cyclic mask-quotient obstruction.
motivation: To characterize when Bernoulli convolutions possess frame measures, which is a fundamental question in harmonic analysis and fractal geometry.
method: The proof introduces a cyclic mask-quotient obstruction adapted to the multi-character structure of consecutive-digit frameworks, and applies it under integer parameter conditions.
result: If the scaling parameters satisfy certain integer relations with a given inequality, then the associated Bernoulli convolution admits no frame measure.
conclusion: The result provides a new necessary condition for the existence of frame measures for this class of self-similar measures, advancing the theory of frame measures.

title: Learning Deterministic And Stochastic Forced Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Tomasz Tyranowski Benedikt Brantner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric framework for learning deterministic and stochastic forced Hamiltonian systems with neural networks. Motivated by the Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and the theory of variational integrators, we introduce the notion of a Lagrange-d'Alembert map and establish a [MATH] convergence theorem for first-order one-step methods. Building on these results, we propose Generalized Forced Hamiltonian Neural Networks (GFHNNs), a class of structure-preserving neural networks obtained by concatenating Lagrange-d'Alembert-Euler maps, and prove a universal approximation theorem for this architecture. We further extend the framework to parameter-dependent systems, leading to Parametric Generalized Forced Hamiltonian Neural Networks (PGFHNNs). By interpreting the multiple Stratonovich integrals appearing in the Stratonovich-Taylor expansion as parameters, the same framework can be applied to stochastic forced Hamiltonian systems whenever information about the underlying Wiener process is available. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed geometric architectures provide significantly improved long-time stability and accuracy compared to non-geometric residual neural networks, while requiring substantially less training data to achieve a comparable level of performance.
tldr: Develops a geometric framework for learning deterministic and stochastic forced Hamiltonian systems with neural networks, introducing Generalized Forced Hamiltonian Neural Networks (GFHNNs) with universal approximation and stability.
motivation: To create structure-preserving neural networks for Hamiltonian systems that provide better long-time stability and accuracy with less training data.
method: Utilizes Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and variational integrators, introduces Lagrange-d'Alembert maps, and concatenates them to form GFHNNs. Extends to parametric and stochastic cases.
result: Demonstrates significantly improved long-time stability and accuracy compared to non-geometric residual networks, requiring less data.
conclusion: The geometric architectures are effective for learning forced Hamiltonian systems, including stochastic ones.

title: Resilience In Trustworthy Wireless Systems
authors: Shixiong Wang, Yumeng Zhang, Hongyu Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resilience has emerged as a fundamental capability for future wireless systems operating in dynamic and uncertain environments. Although resilience has attracted growing attention across academia, industry, and standardization, its conceptual scope, enabling mechanisms, and realization techniques remain fragmented. This paper presents a systematic framework of resilience in wireless systems from a trustworthiness perspective. We first formalize the concept of resilience and distinguish it from related uncertainty-aware terminologies, including reliability, robustness, adaptability, survivability, and recoverability. We then establish a hierarchical framework that organizes resilience into capability dimensions and enabling mechanisms, and that quantifies resilience through different technical aspects. We further use physical links and unmanned aerial vehicle networks as representative wireless scenarios to demonstrate how resilience can be systematically realized through the joint design of architectures, operations, and algorithms. Finally, we examine the fundamental trade-offs in resilience engineering: Improving resilience generally incurs costs in resource efficiency, nominal performance, information acquisition, implementation complexity, and latency.
tldr: This paper proposes a systematic framework for resilience in wireless systems from a trustworthiness perspective.
motivation: Resilience is a key capability for future wireless systems, but its conceptual scope and realization techniques are fragmented across academia, industry, and standardization.
method: The authors formalize the concept of resilience, distinguish it from related terms, and establish a hierarchical framework with capability dimensions and enabling mechanisms. They demonstrate the framework on physical links and UAV networks.
result: The paper provides a structured way to quantify and implement resilience, and highlights fundamental trade-offs such as resource efficiency, nominal performance, and latency.
conclusion: Achieving resilience in wireless systems requires a systematic design approach that balances multiple trade-offs.

title: Sub-optimality Of Marton's Inner Bound For The Two-Receiver Broadcast Channel
authors: Mian Huang, Yanxiao Liu, Yi Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Marton's inner bound, the best-known achievable region for a general discrete memoryless broadcast channel, was proposed by Katalin Marton in 1979, and whether it always achieves the capacity region has remained open since then. In this paper, we establish its strict sub-optimality: we show that the capacity region of some discrete memoryless broadcast channels can be strictly larger than Marton's inner bound.
tldr: 本文证明Marton内界对于两接收者广播信道不是紧的，存在容量区域严格大于Marton内界的离散无记忆广播信道。
motivation: Marton内界自1979年提出以来，一直被认为是最佳可达区域，但其紧性长期未决。本文旨在解决这个开放问题。
method: 通过构造特定的离散无记忆广播信道，并证明其容量区域严格大于Marton内界。
result: 确立了Marton内界的严格次优性。
conclusion: 该结果回答了长期存在的开放问题，表明Marton内界并非总是紧的。

title: A Layered Simplex Architecture For Large Alphabets
authors: Meir Feder, Yaniv Fogel, Ruediger Urbanke
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probability estimation over large alphabets under log loss is a well-studied problem, with celebrated methods such as the Good-Turing estimator. We introduce and study a new Bayesian estimator with four notable properties. First, its construction is exceptionally simple: multiply independent uniform draws from the probability simplex coordinate-wise and renormalize. Depth is the only structural parameter, and averaging over depths eliminates the need to tune it. Second, the regret of the resulting mixture, the excess code length it pays relative to a code that knows the source, admits an explicit and efficiently computable expression. Third, despite its simplicity and lack of tuned constants, the estimator is competitive across a diverse set of synthetic and real-text benchmarks with substantially more specialized methods, including Good-Turing. Fourth, the tractability of its regret allows us to identify scaling laws in data, alphabet size, and depth. For Zipf targets with exponent above one, the regret has a simple reading as long as the sample reveals only a small fraction of the alphabet. It closely matches the description length of the set of discovered symbols, at one bit of code per bit of description, plus a further cost per symbol. The data exponent is therefore the rate at which new symbols are discovered.
tldr: Introduces a simple Bayesian estimator for probability estimation over large alphabets with explicit regret and competitive performance.
motivation: To provide a simple, tunable-free estimator for large-alphabet probability estimation under log loss, with explicit regret and competitive performance.
method: Constructs the estimator by multiplying independent uniform draws from the simplex and renormalizing, with depth as the only parameter, and averages over depths.
result: Derives an explicit regret expression, shows competitive performance against specialized methods including Good-Turing, and identifies scaling laws with alphabet size and depth.
conclusion: The estimator is simple, competitive, and analytically tractable, offering insight into the fundamental limits of large-alphabet estimation.

title: Real Interference Alignment For Active IRS-Aided Systems: A Rate-Profile Learning-Based Approach
authors: Junda Liao, Quanzhong Li, Qi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With additional spatial degrees of freedom provided by the active intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), interference alignment (IA) can be achieved at low cost. In this letter, we propose a real IA scheme for an active IRS-aided system. The proposed scheme only requires the IRS to know the instantaneous channel coefficients under the assumption of blocked direct links. To maximize the achievable sum rate subject to individual minimum rate requirements and transmission power constraints, we propose a rate-profile learning-based algorithm. The algorithm uses offline-trained achievable rate profiles to decouple the original problem into multiple feasibility subproblems, which are then solved by generalized eigenvalue decomposition. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm outperforms the conventional weighted minimum mean square error algorithm, while requiring significantly less program execution time.
tldr: Proposes a real interference alignment scheme for active IRS-aided systems using a rate-profile learning-based approach to maximize sum rate.
motivation: To achieve interference alignment in active IRS systems at low cost, with reduced complexity.
method: Uses offline-trained rate profiles to decouple the optimization problem, solved via generalized eigenvalue decomposition.
result: Outperforms conventional algorithm in sum rate while reducing execution time.
conclusion: Demonstrates effectiveness of learning-based approach for real IA in active IRS systems.

title: String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction And Sample Of Open Problems
authors: Assaf Kfoury
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This document is the result of pulling together small parts of different lecture notes I have written over several decades for first-year graduate-level courses -- typically with the title Formal Methods -- which included many other topics of mathematical logic and theoretical computer science. After combining these materials, I updated the references and adjusted the text to account for progress accomplished in the intervening years. The sample of open problems in the last section is a small collection of special cases that are still unresolved up until the date of this writing.
tldr: A brief introduction to string rewriting systems and a sample of open problems, compiled from lecture notes on formal methods.
motivation: To provide a concise overview of string rewriting systems and highlight unresolved special cases for researchers.
method: Pulling together and updating materials from lecture notes on formal methods and theoretical computer science.
result: A document introducing string rewriting systems and listing a small collection of open problems.
conclusion: This is an expository paper with no new results, serving as a resource for graduate-level study and research.

title: Redactable Blockchains And Polynomial Equations
authors: Alexander Demin, Alexey Ovchinnikov, Vladimir Shpilrain
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop new tools for constructing redactable authenticated data structures with post-quantum security. In our construction, inverting the proposed one-way function means solving a polynomial equation (or a system of polynomial equations) in more than one variable. This is presently considered quantum-safe, i.e., there is no known quantum algorithm that could solve this problem efficiently if parameters are chosen wisely.
tldr: This paper develops redactable authenticated data structures with post-quantum security based on the hardness of solving multivariate polynomial equations.
motivation: To construct redactable blockchains that are secure against quantum attacks, leveraging the presumed intractability of solving polynomial equations.
method: Proposes a one-way function whose inversion reduces to solving polynomial equations in multiple variables, and integrates it into a redactable authenticated data structure.
result: Claims that no known quantum algorithm can efficiently solve the underlying polynomial equations for wisely chosen parameters, providing post-quantum security.
conclusion: The construction offers a new tool for quantum-safe redactable blockchains, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Enhancing Privacy In Federated Learning Via Dual Obfuscation Of Gradients And Training Images
authors: Yuki Itabashi, Hiroto Sawada, Mare Hirose, Shoko Imaizumi, Hitoshi Kiya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training while keeping data locally at each client; however, recent studies have shown that training data can be reconstructed from shared model updates. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dual obfuscation method that enhances robustness against image restoration attacks by jointly obfuscating updated information and training images. The proposed method combines a robustness enhancement technique based on random binary weights, which randomly sets a portion of gradient elements to zero, with an image encryption technique. These techniques provide complementary protection by reducing the amount of original gradient information available to an attacker and the visual interpretability of reconstructed images, respectively. Furthermore, the image encryption technique allows independent keys to be used for each client and each image, avoiding explicit key sharing. Experimental results on an image classification task using a Vision Transformer (ViT) show that the proposed method reduces the visual information recovered by Attention Privacy Leakage (APRIL) under the evaluated settings without causing additional degradation in classification performance beyond that caused by image encryption. Although the proposed combination does not provide an absolute security guarantee, the results demonstrate the potential benefit of combining gradient modification and image encryption for privacy-enhanced federated learning.
tldr: This paper proposes a dual obfuscation method that combines random binary weight gradient modification and image encryption to enhance privacy in federated learning against image reconstruction attacks.
motivation: Federated learning can leak training data from shared gradients, and existing methods are vulnerable to reconstruction attacks; a more robust privacy enhancement is needed.
method: The method jointly obfuscates updated information by randomly setting a portion of gradient elements to zero (random binary weights) and applies image encryption with independent keys per client and per image.
result: Experiments on a Vision Transformer image classification task show the method reduces visual information recovered by Attention Privacy Leakage (APRIL) without causing additional classification performance degradation beyond that from image encryption alone.
conclusion: The combination of gradient modification and image encryption shows potential for privacy-enhanced federated learning, though it does not provide an absolute security guarantee.

title: Lexicographic Combination Of Reduction Pairs (Extended Version)
authors: Nao Hirokawa Teppei Saito
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a simple criterion for combining reduction pairs lexicographically. The criterion is applicable to arbitrary classes of reduction pairs, such as the polynomial interpretation, the matrix interpretation, and the Knuth-Bendix order. In addition, we investigate a variant of the matrix interpretation where the lexicographic order is employed instead of the usual component-wise order. Effectiveness is demonstrated by experiments and examples, including Touzet's Hydra Battle.
tldr: The paper presents a simple criterion for lexicographically combining reduction pairs, applicable to various reduction order classes and demonstrating effectiveness via experiments including Touzet's Hydra Battle.
motivation: To provide a general and effective method for combining reduction pairs in term rewriting, which is essential for proving termination in automated reasoning.
method: The authors introduce a simple criterion for lexicographic combination of reduction pairs, applicable to arbitrary classes such as polynomial interpretations, matrix interpretations, and the Knuth-Bendix order. They also investigate a variant of matrix interpretation using lexicographic order instead of component-wise order.
result: The criterion is demonstrated to be effective through experiments and examples, including Touzet's Hydra Battle, showing practical applicability.
conclusion: The lexicographic combination criterion provides a simple yet powerful tool for combining reduction pairs, enhancing termination proving capabilities in term rewriting systems.

title: RMWorld: Task-Aware Radio World Models With Value-of-Information Guided Multi-Trial Learning For Multi-UAV Communication Control
authors: Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng, Junxi Huan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable multi-UAV communication control depends on predicting which aerial links will serve traffic before measurements are available. Radio world models (radio WMs) make such planning tractable, but their errors are nonuniform: a globally accurate model may still fail along high-demand corridors or association boundaries where rate errors reverse control decisions. This mismatch creates a learning challenge. Link queries must reduce decision-relevant channel uncertainty, while counterfactual trials must be filtered so that biased rollouts do not corrupt the policy. Existing acquisition and model-based control treat these budgets separately, valuing uncertainty, coverage, or optimistic return rather than risk reduction. We present RMWorld, a task-aware radio-WM framework that couples value-of-information channel calibration with credibility-diversity multi-trial selection.
