title: TrustRAG: Blockchain-Enhanced Rag Via Committee-Based Credibility Scoring
authors: Baixiang Liu, Haotian Che, Yuan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) lets Large Language Models (LLMs) pull in up-to-date, domain-specific information instead of relying only on what they were trained on. Yet most RAG systems still draw from centralized databases with limited oversight, making it difficult to verify where a document came from, whether it has been tampered with, or whether it should be trusted at all. This is a serious problem in domains where both the timeliness and accuracy of retrieved content are critical, such as healthcare, finance, logistics, and legal case law, where a wrong or manipulated document can directly lead to bad decisions. We present TrustRAG, a committee-based, blockchain-backed RAG system: before a document is used, it is certified by a committee of domain experts through a zero-knowledge protocol, and the committee's hidden scores are combined via secure multi-party computation into a trust score that any client can verify. These scores, along with the underlying document data, are maintained jointly across chains through hash commitments, so no document or score can be silently altered or dropped, and every ranking can be independently replayed and checked.
tldr: TrustRAG is a blockchain-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation system that uses committee-based credibility scoring to certify document trustworthiness.
motivation: Traditional RAG systems lack oversight and verification of document origin and integrity, which is problematic in high-stakes domains like healthcare, finance, and law.
method: TrustRAG uses a committee of domain experts to certify documents via zero-knowledge protocols, combines hidden scores via secure multi-party computation, and stores scores and documents with hash commitments across chains.
result: The system likely provides verifiable trust, tamper resistance, and replayable document ranking.
conclusion: TrustRAG addresses trust and integrity issues in RAG systems using blockchain and secure computation.

title: A Meta-Study On Replication Papers In Usable Security & Privacy
authors: Christian Mack, Benjamin Berens, Hanna Algedri, Tobias Hilt, Daniela Reimer, Peter Mayer, Melanie Volkamer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The field of usable security and privacy research is a young and expanding field, which is still developing standards for its research, e.g. regarding replications. We used a mixed-method approach, in order to get a better understanding of the current state of replications in the field of usable security and privacy: (1) we examine the Call for Papers of 13 venues spanning security, privacy, and human-computer interaction; (2) we conduct a systematic search for papers reporting replicated user studies published across these venues between 2016 and 2025, yielding 24 relevant publications; (3) we categorized these 24 papers employing the replication taxonomy proposed by Olszewski et al. (2025); (4) we distributed a survey to the authors of these papers to understand their motivations for conducting replications. Our analysis reveals four key insights: (A) Calls for Papers would benefit from clearer guidelines for authors and reviewers regarding replication work; (B) determining what modifications were made relative to the original study proves difficult when reading replication papers; (C) strict exact replications do not exist in our sample. Approximately two-thirds of the 24 studies altered multiple aspects of the original work; (D) temporal and contextual changes affecting results emerged as one of the most frequently cited motivations for replication. Based on these findings, we offer practical recommendations for venues, researchers, and peer reviewers to strengthen replication practices in usable security and privacy research.
tldr: This paper studies the current state of replication studies in usable security and privacy research through a mixed-method approach, finding that replication practices are underdeveloped and offering recommendations.
motivation: To understand the current state of replications in the field of usable security and privacy, which is young and still developing research standards.
method: The authors used a mixed-method approach: examining Call for Papers of relevant venues, systematically searching for replication papers published between 2016 and 2025, categorizing them with a taxonomy, and surveying the authors to understand motivations.
result: Four key insights emerged: clearer guidelines are needed, determining modifications is difficult, strict exact replications are nonexistent (two-thirds altered aspects), and temporal/contextual changes are a frequent motivation for replication.
conclusion: Practical recommendations are provided for venues, researchers, and peer reviewers to strengthen replication practices in usable security and privacy research.

title: Privacy-Preserving Detection Of Rare Disease-Associated Cell Subsets Via Secure Multi-Party Computation
authors: \c{s}. Selcan Magara, Esther Havemann, Debora Jutz, Ali Burak \"unal, Mete Akg\"un
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection of rare disease-associated cell subsets from high-dimensional single-cell measurements is critical for understanding diseases such as leukaemia and viral infections. CellCnn, a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for this task, has demonstrated the ability to identify phenotype-associated cell populations at frequencies as low as 0.01\%. Training such models reliably requires patient cohorts that are larger and more diverse than any single institution can typically assemble, and the underlying single-cell data is too sensitive to share across institutional boundaries under existing privacy regulations. We propose a secure multi-party computation (MPC) framework that enables the training and inference of CellCnn entirely on secret-shared data. This ensures that neither the participants nor the computing servers ever observe raw patient data or intermediate values. Evaluated on benchmark single-cell datasets for cytomegalovirus infection (CMV) and acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), our implementation preserves accuracy close to its plaintext counterpart while outperforming the prior privacy-preserving baseline. In contrast to earlier privacy-preserving approaches that removed components such as ReLU activations and bias terms, our method retains these key parts of the CellCnn architecture and supports accurate analysis without exposing raw patient data.
tldr: The paper presents a secure multi-party computation framework to train and infer CellCnn, a CNN for detecting rare disease-associated cell subsets, without exposing raw patient data.
motivation: Training reliable models requires large, diverse patient cohorts that no single institution can assemble, but sharing sensitive single-cell data across institutions is restricted by privacy regulations.
method: The authors implement CellCnn training and inference entirely on secret-shared data using secure multi-party computation, retaining components like ReLU activations and bias terms that prior privacy-preserving approaches removed.
result: Evaluated on CMV and AML benchmark datasets, the method preserves accuracy close to plaintext and outperforms the prior privacy-preserving baseline.
conclusion: The approach enables privacy-preserving collaborative analysis of rare cell subsets without exposing raw patient data, supporting multi-institutional research.

title: Probabilities Beyond Belnap-Dunn Logic: Dealing With Gaps, Gluts And Reliability
authors: Ver\'onica Borja Macias, Marcelo E. Coniglio, Alejandro Hern\'andez-Tello
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the study of probability functions based on the 6-valued paradefinite (i.e., paraconsistent and paracomplete) logic LETK+. This logic is a powerful and versatile Logic of Evidence and Truth (LET) which is a conservative expansion of both classical logic and FDE. The framework introduced here allowed us to consider gaps, gluts, and reliability (or classicality) of the events, extending the detailed proposal for FDE-based probabilities presented by Klein, Majer, and Rafiee Rad. A distinctive feature of our proposal is the use of twist structure semantics, which gives rise to a natural interpretation of logical probabilities over LETK+ in terms of the three or six regions associated with each formula by a valuation in such models. The LETK+-probability functions are defined axiomatically and semantically, obtaining soundness and completeness results, as one would expect. Finally, conditional probabilities based on LETK+ are also studied. Specifically, both a semantic and a syntactic characterization of Jeffrey's update over LETK+-based probabilities is proposed, showing their equivalence.
tldr: The paper introduces probability functions for the 6-valued paradefinite logic LETK+, handling gaps, gluts, and reliability, with both axiomatic and semantic characterizations and conditional probabilities via Jeffrey's update.
motivation: To extend probability theory to logics that accommodate incomplete and inconsistent information, specifically using LETK+ to deal with gaps, gluts, and reliability.
method: Using twist structure semantics to define logical probabilities, providing axiomatic and semantic definitions, proving soundness and completeness, and studying conditional probabilities with Jeffrey's update.
result: Soundness and completeness results for LETK+-probability functions, and equivalence between semantic and syntactic characterizations of Jeffrey's update.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust approach to probabilities in paraconsistent and paracomplete settings.

title: Measuring What A Specification Determines: A Formal Semantic-Block Model And An Execution-Judged Benchmark
authors: Oleg Grynets, Dmytro Kostetskyi, Vasyl Lyashkevych
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work introduces a formal semantic-block model for specifications and an execution-judged benchmark for evaluating specification quality independently of model capability. A specification is represented as a structure comprising semantic blocks, dependency relations, block-owned rules, decision points, and explicitly open questions, subject to four machine-checkable well-formedness conditions: acyclicity, single ownership, constraint domination, and totality or ambiguity-stop. Determinacy is defined model-theoretically as agreement among all conforming implementations and is estimated empirically through convergence across independent implementers. The model is instantiated on an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration specification containing 18 blocks and 19 dependency edges. Computational validation shows that the five-layer decomposition reduces mean per-task context by approximately 71% through dependency closures, covers 85.5% of the study-defined Oracle construct taxonomy with all identified gaps triaged, is not Pareto-dominated by the tested alternative partitions, and is recovered at the 99.9th percentile from citation-derived edges not used to define the original structure. The benchmark keeps the implementer panel fixed, includes a mandatory no-specification control arm, and uses PostgreSQL 16 and a live Oracle instance as deterministic execution judges. Six designed studies, including three pre-registered manipulations and three diagnostic analyses, further examine specification effects. Repeated runs on a 25-unit subsample reveal an empirical variability floor with a median arm-delta spread of 14.4 percentage points. The results support determinacy as a formal concept but not as a standalone empirical quality metric for the evaluated contemporary LLM implementers.
tldr: This paper introduces a formal semantic-block model and an execution-judged benchmark for evaluating specification quality independently of model capability, applied to an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration task.
motivation: To assess specification quality without confounding by LLM capabilities, the authors propose a formal model and benchmark that rely on empirical convergence across implementations.
method: A semantic-block model with dependency relations and well-formedness conditions is defined; the benchmark fixes an implementer panel, includes a no-specification control, and uses PostgreSQL 16 and a live Oracle instance as judges.
result: The model reduces mean per-task context by ~71%, covers 85.5% of a taxonomy, and is recovered at the 99.9th percentile from citation-derived edges, but determinacy shows a high variability floor (median spread 14.4%).
conclusion: Determinacy works as a formal concept but is not a reliable standalone empirical quality metric for contemporary LLM implementers.

title: Weak Arcs And Applications To The DNA-based Storage Access Problem
authors: Ferdinando Zullo Geertrui van de Voorde
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak arcs are point sets in PG[MATH] meeting every general hyperplane (those are the hyperplanes not going through one of the points given by the standard basis vectors) in at most [MATH] points. In this paper, we study weak arcs together with balanced variants which are contained on the sides of the fundamental simplex. We give an upper bound on the size of weak arcs, characterise the largest balanced quasi-arcs in the plane and construct large balanced quasi-arcs in PG[MATH]. We then use these configurations to build point sets for the random-access problem in DNA-based storage. The constructions are explicit, work over small fields, and attain recovery expectations matching the best known asymptotic bounds.
tldr: This paper studies weak arcs in projective geometries and applies them to construct explicit point sets for random-access in DNA-based storage.
motivation: The paper aims to provide explicit and efficient point set constructions for the DNA storage random-access problem, which has practical importance in data storage.
method: The authors study weak arcs and balanced quasi-arcs in finite projective spaces, prove an upper bound on weak arc size, characterize the largest balanced quasi-arcs in the plane, and construct large balanced quasi-arcs in higher dimensions.
result: They obtain explicit point set constructions over small fields that achieve recovery expectations matching the best known asymptotic bounds.
conclusion: The work contributes to DNA-based storage by offering combinatorial designs that effectively address the random-access problem.

title: Resolving The Generalized Hyperbolicity Conjecture For Shadowing
authors: Mih\'aly Pituk
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that generalized hyperbolicity implies the shadowing property for invertible bounded linear operators on a Banach space. Whether the converse holds has been a central open problem in linear dynamics and has been conjectured to have a positive answer. We show that this conjecture fails on general Banach spaces by constructing a counterexample, whereas it holds on separable Hilbert spaces. The distinction is explained by the gap that may occur on Banach spaces between surjectivity and right invertibility, a gap that disappears on Hilbert spaces. The main ingredients of the proofs are a recent spectral characterization of shadowing in terms of the surjective spectrum and a new characterization of generalized hyperbolicity in terms of right resolvent functions near the unit circle.
tldr: This paper resolves the generalized hyperbolicity conjecture for shadowing, showing it fails on general Banach spaces but holds on separable Hilbert spaces, using spectral and resolvent characterizations.
motivation: The conjecture that shadowing implies generalized hyperbolicity for invertible bounded linear operators was a central open problem in linear dynamics.
method: The author constructs a counterexample on a Banach space and proves the positive result on separable Hilbert spaces, using a spectral characterization of shadowing and a new characterization of generalized hyperbolicity via right resolvent functions.
result: The conjecture fails on general Banach spaces due to the gap between surjectivity and right invertibility, but it holds on separable Hilbert spaces where this gap disappears.
conclusion: The validity of the conjecture depends on the underlying space, highlighting a fundamental difference between general and Hilbert spaces in linear dynamics.

title: On The Value Function Of Infinite-Horizon Optimal Control Of Piecewise Affine Systems
authors: Francesco Cordiano, Kanghui He, Bart de Schutter
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the value function in constrained infinite-time optimal control (CITOC) problems of piecewise affine (PWA) systems, with [MATH] or [MATH] stage cost. Existing works, such as [1], establish that the resulting value function is PWA in the state. However, existing results do not analyze whether the value function is a proper PWA function, i.e., with a finite number of affine pieces over compact sets, or whether the number of pieces can be infinite. We show that the latter case is indeed possible by means of an explicit example, which is also instrumental in establishing rigorous and easily verifiable sufficient conditions that ensure that the resulting value function is a proper PWA function. Our theoretical findings complement well-known results, e.g., the linear-quadratic case, and serve as support for recent learning-based control schemes for PWA systems. Throughout the paper, the proposed results are illustrated by means of a numerical example.
tldr: This paper studies the structure of the value function for constrained infinite-time optimal control of piecewise affine systems, showing that it can have infinitely many pieces and providing conditions for a proper PWA form.
motivation: Existing results establish that the value function is piecewise affine but do not analyze whether the number of affine pieces is finite; this paper addresses that gap.
method: The authors construct an explicit example demonstrating infinite pieces, then derive sufficient conditions ensuring a proper PWA value function, and illustrate results with a numerical example.
result: The value function for such optimal control problems can indeed have infinitely many affine pieces, but specific conditions guarantee a finite number.
conclusion: The findings complement known results and support learning-based control schemes for PWA systems.

title: To Control Or Not To Control
authors: Odysseas Kanavetas, Camiel M. P. Koopmans, Floske M. Spieksma
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a model with control vacations instead of standard queueing control systems with permanent control. The researched model is an M/M/1 queue with temporary periods of service rate control with two available service rates. After a control period of exponentially distributed length, a control vacation is initiated during which a fixed service rate [MATH] is used. The start of the next control period needs to be scheduled directly at a certain cost. We will use the Markov Decision Process from Kanavetas et al. arXiv:2605.31573 to find a sufficient condition that ensures that the average expected cost can be reduced w.r.t. the model that only uses the fixed service rate. Under this condition we will use properties of this related process to construct a cost reducing policy. The process with control vacations under specific policies induces a renewal reward process. We use a Tauberian theorem to relate the average expected cost of this renewal reward process to a vanishing discount method and analytically determine a lower bound of the average expected cost reduction. Finally, we study the actual attained average cost reduction for these policies through simulation.
tldr: Introduces a M/M/1 queue with control vacations and shows that scheduling control periods can reduce average cost under certain conditions.
motivation: To determine whether temporary service rate control periods can be more cost-effective than permanent control in queueing systems.
method: Uses a Markov Decision Process model, analyzes the renewal reward process under specific policies, applies a Tauberian theorem for asymptotic cost analysis, and verifies via simulation.
result: Derives a sufficient condition for cost reduction and a lower bound on average cost reduction; simulation confirms the analytical findings.
conclusion: The proposed control vacation policies can achieve cost savings compared to permanent control, provided certain conditions are met.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks As Fast Surrogate Models For Electrochemical Flow Reactors
authors: Eric Fern\'andez-Garc\'ia, Miguel Modestino, Sergio Maldonado
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a physics-informed neural network (PINN) for modeling a transient two-dimensional electrochemical flow reactor with diffusion, migration, convection, and nonlinear anodic Butler--Volmer kinetics. The model is trained without labeled concentration data by embedding the governing transport equation and all initial and boundary conditions into a composite loss function. Spatial and temporal coordinates together with anodic overpotential, temperature, inlet concentration, maximum flow velocity, and diffusivity are used as inputs, allowing the network to predict concentration fields over a broad operating domain. Validation against finite-difference-based solutions shows strong agreement for representative transient and near-steady cases, with a mean relative space--time error of [MATH] (sub-percent level) across the conditioning domain. PINN inference is faster than a traditional finite difference solver by a factor of [MATH], thus reducing runtime by [MATH]. Generalization tests further show that the surrogate remains robust under in-domain boundary-focused sampling and controlled extrapolation, although anodic overpotential is the most challenging parameter due to its exponential effect on interfacial kinetics. The results indicate that physics-informed neural networks can serve as accurate and efficient parametric surrogates for electrochemical transport problems and provide a foundation for low-computational-cost digital-twin modeling of electrochemical flow reactors.
tldr: This paper presents a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate model for fast and accurate prediction of concentration fields in an electrochemical flow reactor.
motivation: The authors aim to reduce computational cost of simulating electrochemical flow reactors by developing a fast surrogate model that embeds governing physics without labeled data.
method: A PINN is trained by incorporating the transport equations and boundary/initial conditions into the loss function, with inputs including spatial and temporal coordinates and operating parameters.
result: The PINN achieves sub-percent error compared to finite-difference solutions and is significantly faster, although performance degrades for high anodic overpotential.
conclusion: PINNs can serve as efficient parametric surrogates for electrochemical transport problems, enabling digital-twin modeling.

title: The 1908 Tunguska Event In Data Of The Nearest Weather Station
authors: Andrei Ol'khovatov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a continuation of a series of works, devoted to various aspects of the 1908 Tunguska event. In this paper data is discussed from a weather station in the settlement of Kezma. This weather station was the nearest one to the epicenter of the 1908 Tunguska event. The station was about 215 km southwards from the epicenter. Also eyewitness accounts from Kezhma and some places on the Angara River are considered. The paper demonstrates the diversity of optical manifestations of the 1908 Tunguska event reported from Kezhma and its surroundings. A note by the observer of the weather station in Kezhma, concerning, in particular, the appearance of the two huge fiery circles is very important. The weather log of the weather station shows that the Tunguska event occurred during the sharp increase in cloud cover and deteriorating weather. At the beginning of July, rains and thunderstorms, including hail, began according to the weather log. In the opinion of the author, the data of the Kezhma weather station and the eyewitness accounts are in agreement with the geophysical interpretation of the 1908 Tunguska event. In any case, the meteorological factor is an important aspect of the Tunguska event, and so it deserves detailed research.
tldr: This paper analyzes weather station data and eyewitness accounts from the 1908 Tunguska event, arguing for a geophysical interpretation and highlighting meteorological aspects.
motivation: To better understand the 1908 Tunguska event by examining the nearest weather station data and local eyewitness reports.
method: Reviews historical weather logs from the Kezhma station and eyewitness accounts from the Angara River region, correlating them with the event's optical manifestations.
result: The weather log shows a sharp increase in cloud cover and deteriorating weather around the event, with rains and thunderstorms beginning shortly after, and eyewitness accounts describe unusual optical phenomena like two huge fiery circles.
conclusion: The meteorological data and eyewitness accounts support a geophysical interpretation of the Tunguska event, emphasizing the role of atmospheric conditions.

title: Outer Contact Billiards
authors: Connor Jackman Ana Chavez Caliz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce outer contact billiards as an odd dimensional counterpart to outer symplectic billiards. Until now, outer billiards have only been considered in even dimensional symplectic vector spaces. By projectivizing outer symplectic billiards, we obtain outer contact billiards, where the affine midpoint condition descends to its projective analog, namely harmonic conjugation. We prove that outer contact billiards generate contactomorphisms. For quadratic surfaces in [MATH], we show that the correspondence is completely integrable: its domain is foliated by invariant quadrics and, on each leaf, the dynamics is determined by the iteration of an explicit linear transformation. We also establish two rigidity results for periodic trajectories: outer contact billiards admit no 3-periodic orbits and, among quadratic tables, only one admits 4-periodic orbits.
tldr: This paper introduces outer contact billiards as an odd-dimensional analogue of outer symplectic billiards, proving they generate contactomorphisms and have integrable dynamics on quadratic surfaces.
motivation: To extend the theory of outer billiards to odd-dimensional contact geometry, since previous work only considered even-dimensional symplectic spaces.
method: Projectivize outer symplectic billiards to obtain outer contact billiards, using harmonic conjugation as the projective midpoint condition, and analyze the resulting contactomorphisms and dynamics on quadratic surfaces.
result: The authors prove that outer contact billiards yield contactomorphisms, show complete integrability on quadratic surfaces via invariant quadrics and linear transformations, and establish rigidity results including the absence of 3-periodic orbits and uniqueness of a quadratic table with 4-periodic orbits.
conclusion: The paper introduces a new class of billiards with rich geometric structure, demonstrating integrability and rigidity properties that may have applications in dynamical systems and contact topology.

title: Trustworthy Mobile Edge Caching: A Blockchain Approach To Mitigate Malicious Nodes And Incentivize Cache Sharing
authors: Motahare Ebrahimi, Nastooh Taheri Javan, Seyedakbar Mostafavi, Fatemeh Pakzaban
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As mobile network traffic continues to grow, content caching on edge servers is critical for reducing latency. However, challenges such as malicious edge servers that may delete or manipulate cached content, along with the limited capacity of these servers, need to be addressed. To overcome the capacity limitations, helper mobile nodes can contribute their cache resources. However, due to their selfish behavior, an incentive mechanism is necessary to encourage resource sharing. Additionally, these helper nodes can also be malicious. This paper proposes a blockchain-based trust management mechanism that addresses these challenges by accurately identifying trustworthy edge servers and mobile nodes. The proposed mechanism calculates both direct and indirect trust using smart contracts, ensuring that malicious nodes are effectively filtered out. Trustworthiness is determined based on mobile node satisfaction with the quality of service, and trust data is securely stored on the blockchain. To combat node selfishness, a reward mechanism is introduced to incentivize cache sharing. Furthermore, a blockchain-based authentication mechanism protects against node impersonation. Our approach optimizes trust, cache capacity, and cost efficiency while considering mobile node mobility, energy consumption, and computational power constraints during the consensus process. Simulation results show that the proposed method can accurately distinguish between honest and malicious servers, even with a 10% noise in data.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain-based trust and incentive mechanism for mobile edge caching to handle malicious nodes and encourage cache sharing.
motivation: Mobile network traffic growth requires efficient caching, but malicious edge servers and selfish helper nodes threaten reliability; need to manage trust and incentivize sharing.
method: Uses smart contracts on a blockchain to compute direct and indirect trust scores for edge servers and mobile nodes, and implements a reward mechanism to incentivize cache sharing, while also including authentication to prevent impersonation.
result: Simulations show the method can accurately distinguish honest and malicious servers even with 10% noise, and optimizes trust, cache capacity, and cost efficiency.
conclusion: The blockchain-based approach effectively enhances trust and incentivization in mobile edge caching, though it is unrelated to quantum information research.

title: Harp: Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking With Preference-Adaptive Fusion For Query-Based Cve Prioritization
authors: Haochen Liu, Zhengzhang Chen, Haoyu Wang, Yanchi Liu, Jundong Li, Haifeng Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vulnerability prioritization is inherently preference dependent, since the same CVE can receive different remediation priority under different operational preference scenarios. Existing scoring systems and ranking methods typically assume a fixed criterion. In practice, organizations already operate under a preference scenario, but this preference is often implicit and difficult to express as a written prompt instruction, while triage queries usually do not encode it. Past validated triage cases under the current scenario are more readily available. We study query-based CVE prioritization in this setting and propose HARP, a graph-grounded multi-view framework that ranks candidates from a natural-language query together with a support bank of historical labeled examples from the current preference scenario, without requiring an explicit textual summary of that scenario. HARP retrieves evidence from a vulnerability knowledge graph, scores candidates with policy-conditioned global, enterprise, and user views, and fits view-fusion weights from sampled supports. Experiments across three preference scenarios and multiple backbone LLMs show that HARP outperforms multiple baselines, expressing our method's effectiveness.
tldr: HARP is a graph-grounded multi-view framework for query-based CVE prioritization that adapts to implicit preference scenarios using historical labeled examples and a knowledge graph.
motivation: Existing vulnerability prioritization methods assume fixed criteria, but organizations have implicit preferences that are hard to express explicitly; past validated triage cases can be used to infer these preferences.
method: HARP retrieves evidence from a vulnerability knowledge graph, scores candidates with policy-conditioned global, enterprise, and user views, and fits view-fusion weights from sampled supports.
result: Experiments across three preference scenarios and multiple backbone LLMs show HARP outperforms several baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness.
conclusion: The method effectively addresses preference-dependent CVE prioritization without requiring explicit preference summaries, leveraging historical data and knowledge graphs.

title: Hippogriff: A Semantic Approach To Uniting Core And Modules
authors: Sam Staton Owen Lynch
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we introduce Hippogriff, a language with a module system that unifies syntax between the core level and the module level. Hippogriff's type theory is dependent, with modularity features enabled via a universe of small types, but Hippogriff still supports general recursion without making typechecking nonterminating. This paper contains two halves. In the first half, we describe Hippogriff and its implementation. In the second half, we build categorical semantics for our use of dependent types that justify the use of general recursion at the value level. Specifically, we use an extension of the second-order generalized algebraic theory framework to include a synthetic phase distinction, and this allows us to make a mathematical connection between dependent type theories and split-context type theories (like System F). Included as supplements are a Haskell implementation of Hippogriff and an appendix describing the full type theory of Hippogriff using a second-order generalized algebraic theory with phase distinction.
tldr: Hippogriff is a programming language with a module system that unifies core and module syntax using dependent types and categorical semantics.
motivation: To unify the syntax between core and module levels and support general recursion while keeping typechecking terminating.
method: Introduce Hippogriff with dependent types and a universe of small types, and provide categorical semantics using an extension of second-order generalized algebraic theories with a phase distinction.
result: They demonstrate a language that supports general recursion and modularity without nonterminating typechecking, and provide mathematical foundations via categorical semantics.
conclusion: The work shows that dependent type theories and split-context type theories can be connected through phase distinction, enabling a unified approach.

title: Second-Order Continuum Model For Disordered Traffic
authors: Shashank Rajput, Venkatesan Kanagaraj, Martin Treiber, Gowri Asaithambi, Ostap Okhrin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, a two-dimensional second-order macroscopic traffic flow model is proposed to capture the complex dynamics of disordered traffic by explicitly incorporating coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions. The framework extends the classical continuity equation to two spatial dimensions and introduces acceleration equations consisting of self-driven, interaction-induced, and road-boundary-related components. The macroscopic longitudinal acceleration is formulated based on the Full Velocity Difference Model (FVDM), while lateral dynamics are governed by interaction principles consistent with the Optimal Velocity Model (OVM). The explicit inclusion of road-boundary effects enables the representation of vehicle confinement and space-sharing behavior that are essential in lane-free and weakly lane-disciplined traffic systems. The model is examined through a series of numerical experiments in which longitudinal and lateral dynamics are analysed individually as well as simultaneously within a coupled two-dimensional setting under a range of initial conditions, including transitions between free-flow, medium congestion, and heavy congestion, and different lateral density configurations. The simulations demonstrate the model's ability to reproduce key traffic features such as shockwave propagation, lateral dispersion, vehicle rearrangement, and stable density evolution across the road width. The numerical scheme, based on upwind and Lax-Friedrichs discretisations, ensures stable solutions of the coupled partial differential equations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust macroscopic description of disordered traffic and offers a consistent basis for analysing two-dimensional vehicular flow dynamics.
tldr: The paper proposes a two-dimensional second-order macroscopic traffic flow model for disordered traffic.
motivation: To capture the complex dynamics of disordered traffic by explicitly incorporating coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions.
method: Extends the classical continuity equation to two spatial dimensions, using the Full Velocity Difference Model for longitudinal dynamics and the Optimal Velocity Model for lateral dynamics, with road-boundary effects.
result: Numerical experiments show the model reproduces shockwave propagation, lateral dispersion, vehicle rearrangement, and stable density evolution across the road width.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust macroscopic description of disordered traffic and a basis for analyzing two-dimensional vehicular flow dynamics.

title: From The Half-Order Recurrence To General Fractional-Order Differentiation On Monomials: Functional Continuation And Operator Composition
authors: Davit Kapanadze
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work develops a general-order fractional differentiation operator on monomials from the discrete half-order coefficient structure established in Part I. Starting from the one-step transfer law of the integer coefficient family, the discrete coefficient relation is continued to a real argument and a canonical Gamma-functional form is selected under the stated normalization and regularity requirements. The operator order is then extended beyond one half by dividing the first derivative into equal operator steps, leading from orders 1/m and k/m to general rational and real orders. The resulting coefficient is independently verified through the addition law for operator orders on the monomial system, subject to the requirement that all intermediate expressions in the composition are defined. On the corresponding parameter domain, the construction yields the standard Gamma-ratio monomial formula for fractional differentiation. For nonnegative integer orders it reduces to ordinary repeated differentiation, while for positive non-integer orders it agrees at the monomial level with the left-sided Riemann-Liouville formula with lower limit 0. Its relation to the Caputo operator is also discussed, including the distinction for constants and low-degree polynomial terms. The aim is not to introduce a new classical fractional derivative, but to provide a constructive algebraic-operator route from a discrete coefficient law to the general fractional-order monomial formula, clarifying the roles of functional continuation, Gamma normalization, and operator composition.
tldr: This paper constructs a general fractional-order differentiation operator on monomials via functional continuation and operator composition, yielding the standard Gamma-ratio monomial formula.
motivation: To provide a constructive algebraic-operator route from a discrete half-order coefficient law to the general fractional-order monomial formula, clarifying the roles of functional continuation, Gamma normalization, and operator composition.
method: The discrete coefficient relation is continued to a real argument, a canonical Gamma-functional form is selected, and the operator order is extended to rational and real orders by dividing the first derivative into equal operator steps. The result is verified using the addition law for operator orders.
result: The construction yields the standard Gamma-ratio monomial formula for fractional differentiation, reduces to ordinary repeated differentiation for nonnegative integers, and agrees with left-sided Riemann-Liouville on monomials for positive non-integer orders.
conclusion: The paper does not introduce a new fractional derivative but provides an algebraic constructive derivation that clarifies the underpinnings of standard fractional monomial formulas and discusses relations to Caputo operators.

title: A Rock-paper-scissors Mandelbrot Set
authors: Charlotte Aten
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The titular object of this paper is an analogue of the Mandelbrot set over the 3-dimensional real algebra whose multiplication is the bilinear extension of the rock-paper-scissors operation. In order to study the dynamics of the mappings [MATH] in this setting, a notion of holomorphy for functions on general finite-dimensional real algebras is introduced. Under a mild assumption it is shown that for such algebras holomorphy is always equivalent to solving a finite system of linear first-order PDEs generalizing the Cauchy-Riemann equations. Code is provided for generating animations of these fractals and for exploring them in a video game format.
tldr: This paper defines a Mandelbrot analogue over a 3D real algebra with rock-paper-scissors multiplication, introducing holomorphy for general finite-dimensional real algebras and showing it is equivalent to solving a system of PDEs.
motivation: The study aims to analyze the dynamics of mappings on a novel real algebra with a rock-paper-scissors operation, extending fractal generation to this setting.
method: A notion of holomorphy for functions on finite-dimensional real algebras is introduced, generalizing the Cauchy-Riemann equations, and applied to the rock-paper-scissors algebra.
result: Under a mild condition, holomorphy is proven equivalent to solving a finite system of linear first-order PDEs, and code is provided for generating animations and a video game exploring the fractals.
conclusion: The paper establishes a framework for holomorphic functions on real algebras and uses it to define a new type of Mandelbrot set, with computational tools for visualization.

title: The Number Of Limit Cycles Of Piecewise Linear Li\'enard Systems
authors: Hebai Chen, Zhijie Li, Rui Zhang, Xiang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the planar Li\'{e}nard differential system [MATH], [MATH], where [MATH] is a piecewise linear function, Tonnelier (SIAM J. Appl. Math., 2002) conjectured that the maximum number of limit cycles of the system is [MATH] when [MATH] has [MATH] fold points and no jump points, and [MATH] when [MATH] has [MATH] jump points and no fold points. This conjecture was confirmed by Llibre et al. (J. Nonlinear Sci., 2015) (resp. Chen et al. (J. London Math. Soc., 2026a)) when [MATH] has one fold point and no jump points (resp. two fold points). More recently, Chen et al. (J. London Math. Soc., 2026b) proved that the conjecture is correct when [MATH] has no fold points and one jump point. All other cases remain open. Here we verify that the lower bound for the maximum number of limit cycles of the system can be [MATH] when [MATH] has only [MATH] fold points, and [MATH] when [MATH] has only [MATH] jump points, thereby confirming the lower bound part of Tonnelier's conjecture. Moreover, when [MATH] has [MATH] jump points and [MATH] fold points, [MATH], we also show that the system can have [MATH] limit cycles. In addition, a complete classification of the {dynamics} near infinity for this class of systems is provided.
tldr: This paper studies the maximum number of limit cycles in piecewise linear Liénard systems, confirming lower bounds for Tonnelier's conjecture.
motivation: To resolve an open conjecture about the maximum number of limit cycles for piecewise linear Liénard systems with given fold and jump points.
method: Uses analytical and qualitative methods from dynamical systems theory, including analysis of dynamics near infinity and construction of systems with specified numbers of limit cycles.
result: Confirms the lower bound part of Tonnelier's conjecture for systems with only fold points or only jump points, and shows additional limit cycles in mixed cases.
conclusion: Provides partial confirmation of the conjecture and a classification of dynamics near infinity, advancing the understanding of piecewise linear Liénard systems.

title: An Exact Structural Identity And Its Normal Form Consequences In A Modified Leslie--Gower Model
authors: Roberto Albarr\'an-Garc\'ia, Martha Alvarez-Ram\'irez, Marco Polo Garc\'ia-Rivera
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zhao and Zhao (2026) established a codimension-four Bogdanov--Takens singularity in a modified Leslie--Gower predator--prey model through a recursive normal form computation. We show that the nonlinear coefficients governing the restriction of the reduced system to the singularity's distinguished eigendirection are not independent. Instead, a single exact rational identity, already present in the transformed equations, generates the entire family of pure Taylor coefficients and proves that their simultaneous vanishing is an exact all orders property rather than a finite-order coincidence. We further show that this structural identity propagates through the planar Bogdanov--Takens normal form algorithm of Kuznetsov (2005). Although the pure coefficients vanish identically, the corresponding normal form coefficients are generated by mixed quadratic interactions. This leads to an explicit characterization of the degenerate Bogdanov--Takens locus and reduces the search for higher-order Bogdanov--Takens degeneracies to a single explicit algebraic condition.
tldr: This paper reveals an exact rational identity among nonlinear coefficients in a modified Leslie-Gower model, proving that the vanishing of pure Taylor coefficients is an exact all-orders property and simplifying the degenerate Bogdanov-Takens locus characterization.
motivation: To understand and simplify the analysis of a codimension-four Bogdanov-Takens singularity in a predator-prey model, and to explain why certain coefficients vanish.
method: The authors analyze the transformed equations, identify a structural identity among the nonlinear coefficients, and propagate it through Kuznetsov's planar Bogdanov-Takens normal form algorithm.
result: They show that pure coefficients vanish identically due to the structural identity, while normal form coefficients arise from mixed quadratic interactions, yielding an explicit algebraic condition for higher-order degeneracies.
conclusion: The structural identity fully characterizes the degenerate Bogdanov-Takens locus and reduces the search for higher-order degeneracies to a single algebraic condition.

title: Open Cover Specification Property And Chaos
authors: Shweta Wadhwani, Devender Kumar, A R Prasannan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the open cover specification property and its role in the study of topological dynamical systems. We show that this property is a topological invariant and a natural extension of the classical topological specification property from uniform spaces to general topological spaces, and that it is preserved under infinite products with compositions. We further prove that on regular spaces, the strong open cover specification property implies Devaney chaos, and that on locally compact, first countable Hausdorff spaces, it guarantees both distributional chaos and Li Yorke chaos. These results demonstrate the significance of the open cover specification property in linking topological structure with dynamical complexity.
tldr: This paper investigates the open cover specification property in topological dynamical systems and proves it implies various types of chaos under certain conditions.
motivation: To understand how topological properties relate to dynamical complexity, specifically extending the classical specification property to general topological spaces.
method: The authors prove theorems showing the open cover specification property is a topological invariant and preserved under infinite products, and then demonstrate its implications for chaos.
result: They show that the strong open cover specification property implies Devaney chaos on regular spaces, and distributional and Li-Yorke chaos on locally compact, first countable Hausdorff spaces.
conclusion: The results highlight the open cover specification property as a key link between topological structure and dynamical complexity.

title: High-Multiplicity Flexible Job Shops: From Exact Recurrent Fluid Attainment To Structure-Guided Finite-Horizon Scheduling
authors: Wenjun Zheng, Wei Qu, Weilin Cai, Jianfeng Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-multiplicity flexible job shops involve many copies of a small set of job types that must be scheduled on alternative machines. Fluid relaxations provide scalable workload lower bounds, but their fractional machine allocations do not define feasible schedules for individual jobs. We show that, after a suitable finite scaling, an optimal fluid allocation can be realized exactly by a feasible repeating discrete schedule. The construction scales the fluid allocation to integer operation counts, places the resulting operations in nonoverlapping machine intervals, repeats this arrangement, and links operations across repetitions into individual jobs without moving any interval, thereby enforcing job precedence while preserving machine feasibility. For growing finite instances with the same job-type composition, even with a fixed number of extra jobs, the gap between the optimal makespan and the fluid lower bound remains bounded by a constant; hence the relative gap vanishes as the instance grows. Guided by this repeated structure, we develop type-based cyclic template replay (TCTR), which searches job-type templates using an optimization model whose size does not grow with the number of job copies and replays the selected template on the full instance. On 676 multiplicity-expanded public flexible-job-shop instances, TCTR is feasible in every case and achieves a 1.54% mean gap to the fluid lower bound, compared with 5.32% for a job-indexed adaptive large-neighborhood search and 6.18% for a hybrid genetic algorithm.
tldr: The paper develops a method to realize optimal fluid allocations exactly in high-multiplicity flexible job shops, achieving near-optimal schedules with bounded gaps.
motivation: Fluid relaxations provide lower bounds but not feasible schedules; the authors aim to construct feasible schedules that tightly track the fluid bound.
method: They scale fluid allocations to integer counts, arrange operations in nonoverlapping intervals, and link them into jobs via a repeating pattern; then they introduce TCTR, a template-based scheduling search.
result: On 676 instances, TCTR achieves a 1.54% mean gap to the fluid lower bound, outperforming existing heuristics.
conclusion: The repeated structure enables efficient, near-optimal scheduling for large multiplicity job shops.

title: Sharp Dimension Bounds For Spline Spaces Over T-meshes With Highest Order Of Smoothness
authors: Falai Chen Bingru Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dimension of a polynomial spline space of bi-degree [MATH] over a T-mesh [MATH] with the highest order of smoothness [MATH] depends on both mesh topology and geometric configurations. Under the assumption that the T-connected components of the T-mesh [MATH] contain no vanishable T [MATH]-edges, we develop explicit upper and lower bounds of the dimension of the polynomial spline space. By introducing a decoupling technique within the completely non-diagonalizable component (CNDC) of the T-mesh [MATH], we separate tightly coupled multi-vertex constraints and transform global conformality conditions into localized linear equations along each interior large edge. Based on the decoupling technique, a new dimension formula of the polynomial spline space is then presented, and from which sharp upper and lower bounds of the dimension are obtained. The bounds are sharp in the sense that different geometric realizations of T-meshes with the same topology can attain the lower and upper bounds for the dimension of the polynomial spline space. We further prove that the new formula is consistent with Mourrain's homological dimension formula, and a sharper lower bound is obtained by our method.
tldr: The paper presents explicit upper and lower bounds for the dimension of polynomial spline spaces over T-meshes with highest order of smoothness, using a decoupling technique.
motivation: The dimension of spline spaces over T-meshes depends on both mesh topology and geometry, and existing formulas are not sharp. The authors aim to provide tight bounds and a new dimension formula.
method: They introduce a decoupling technique within completely non-diagonalizable components (CNDC) of the T-mesh to separate tightly coupled multi-vertex constraints, transforming global conformality conditions into localized linear equations along interior large edges. They then derive a new dimension formula and prove consistency with Mourrain's homological formula.
result: They obtain sharp upper and lower bounds that are attainable by different geometric realizations of T-meshes with the same topology, and a sharper lower bound than existing methods.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of spline space dimensions over T-meshes, providing theoretically tight and practically useful bounds.

title: Sets Of Nice Recurrence Are Partition Regular
authors: Jonathan Chapman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A set of positive integers [MATH] is called a set of nice recurrence if for any measure preserving system [MATH], for all measurable [MATH], and each [MATH], there exists [MATH] such that [MATH]. Answering a long-standing question of Bergelson, we show that sets of nice recurrence have the following Ramsey property: any finite colouring of a set of nice recurrence admits a monochromatic set of nice recurrence.
tldr: The paper proves that any finite coloring of a set of nice recurrence contains a monochromatic set of nice recurrence.
motivation: Answering a long-standing question of Bergelson about the Ramsey property of sets of nice recurrence.
method: The paper likely employs ergodic theory and combinatorial Ramsey theory to establish the partition regularity.
result: It is shown that sets of nice recurrence are partition regular: any finite coloring admits a monochromatic set of nice recurrence.
conclusion: The question is answered affirmatively, establishing a Ramsey-type property for sets of nice recurrence.

title: A Comprehensive p-VEM Framework For Advanced Variable Stiffness Plates With Arbitrary Shapes
authors: Paola Pia Foligno, Daniele Boffi, Fabio Credali, Riccardo Vescovini
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive, high-order (p-version) Virtual Element Method (VEM) framework for the structural analysis of innovative variable stiffness plates. VEM is particularly suited for complex configurations due to its ability to handle arbitrary polygonal meshes, including curved edges. However, its mathematical formulation may hinder its spread in the engineering community. This work illustrates a formulation with an accessible implementation using well-known FEM notation and integrating at the same time a set of new advanced capabilities. Specifically, both standard stabilized and advanced self-stabilized strategies are adopted. To further improve the robustness of VEM in the presence of variable coefficients, polynomial projections taking into account the coefficients are employed. This approach is referred to as Variable Coefficients-VEM approach (VC-VEM). This unified framework is applied to linear static, free-vibration, and buckling analyses, and validated against analytical solutions and numerical benchmarks. In particular, plates with cutouts and problems featuring high-gradient solutions are investigated, demonstrating that the proposed comprehensive approach provides a flexible and ready-to-implement tool for advanced structural design.
tldr: A high-order Virtual Element Method framework for structural analysis of variable stiffness plates with arbitrary shapes, validated against benchmarks.
motivation: To make VEM accessible and robust for engineering users by providing a ready-to-implement formulation that handles complex plate geometries and variable stiffness.
method: Formulates a p-version VEM using standard FEM notation, incorporating stabilized and self-stabilized strategies and variable coefficient projections (VC-VEM), and applies it to static, vibration, and buckling analyses.
result: The framework is validated against analytical solutions and numerical benchmarks, demonstrating flexibility and accuracy for plates with cutouts and high-gradient solutions.
conclusion: The proposed comprehensive VEM approach provides a flexible, ready-to-implement tool for advanced structural design of variable stiffness plates.

title: Incident-Data Robustness Analysis Of The Owasp Top 10 For Llm Applications (2026): How A Community-Expert Ranking Holds Up Against A Large-Scale Llm Incident Corpus
authors: Steve Wilson Kyriakos "rock" Lambros
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications ranks the risks that a community of security practitioners judges most important. We ask a narrower question: checked against the record of real incidents, does that expert ranking agree with the data? We assembled a large-scale corpus of LLM-security incidents (7,714 snapshotted and 6,639 labeled against the 20-entry taxonomy) drawn from CVE, GHSA, OSV, and AIAAIC, and derived an incident-based ranking with a Bayesian measurement-error model that corrects each category's count for classifier precision and recall. The 2026 candidate list blends the two signals at fixed weights, 0.75 on the expert vote and 0.25 on the data, so the corpus corrects the consensus without overturning it. The agreement between the two rankings is weak: Cohen's [MATH], with a 90% interval that crosses zero. The expert ranking is nonetheless robust. A pre-registered bake-off of four frontier classifiers returns no winner. None beats the incidence floor's balanced accuracy of 0.863. A ground-truth check leaves the floor's ordering (Spearman [MATH] against held-out truth) in place. This is an exploratory analysis by two working-group members, not the official OWASP release, and it does not supersede the official list or process.
tldr: This paper evaluates whether the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications expert ranking aligns with real LLM security incidents using a large-scale corpus and Bayesian modeling, finding weak agreement but robustness of the expert list.
motivation: To test if community-expert risk rankings for LLM applications correspond to actual incident data, which is crucial for effective prioritization in security.
method: Assembled 7,714 LLM-security incidents, labeled 6,639 against a taxonomy, used a Bayesian measurement-error model to correct counts, and compared the incident-based ranking with the expert ranking via Cohen's kappa and classifier performance.
result: Weak agreement between expert and data rankings (Cohen's kappa interval crosses zero); expert ranking remains robust, with no classifier beating the incidence floor's balanced accuracy of 0.863.
conclusion: The expert ranking is broadly robust despite weak data agreement, suggesting it captures latent risks not yet fully reflected in incidents, and the analysis is exploratory, not an official OWASP release.

title: Abeat: Efficient And Anonymous Encryption For ABE-based Dynamic Group Communication
authors: Hongmiao Yu, Silas Richelson, Jiachen Chen, K. K. Ramakrishnan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidential communication among a dynamic group of participants that ensures flexible and efficient many-to- many communication is highly desired capability. We leverage attribute-based encryption (ABE) for confidential group communication and enhance it by a graph-based namespace to create an efficient framework that allows groups to be formed and changed dynamically. In this paper, we focus on the important additional need to maintain the anonymity of recipients of a message, when using ABE for group communication for a variety of usage scenarios (e.g., emergency response). We propose ABEAT, an efficient and anonymous dynamic group communication system that also minimizes overhead on receivers who are not the intended recipients of a message. In ABEAT, we propose a new anonymous KP-ABE approach to maintain recipient anonymity. ABEAT hides the clear attribute in the ciphertext of KP-ABE, and also prevents several attacks that seek to break anonymity. ABEAT provides fast recipient verification, dramatically lowering the decryption overhead for non-recipients by more than a factor of 90 versus the current state of the art such as hidden vector encryption (HVE). In fact, it is even 40% less than FABEO, which offers no anonymity.
tldr: This paper presents ABEAT, an anonymous attribute-based encryption scheme for efficient and confidential communication in dynamic groups.
motivation: Ensuring recipient anonymity in group communication using attribute-based encryption is challenging, especially for dynamic groups and emergency scenarios.
method: ABEAT uses a graph-based namespace and a new anonymous KP-ABE approach that hides ciphertext attributes, enabling fast recipient verification and reducing decryption overhead.
result: ABEAT reduces non-recipient decryption overhead by over 90% compared to hidden vector encryption and is 40% more efficient than FABEO while offering anonymity.
conclusion: ABEAT provides an efficient, anonymous, and dynamic group communication framework with practical performance improvements.

title: Aray: Deterministic-First Synthesis Of Benign Artifacts For Yara Validation
authors: Emanuel C. A. Valente (ifood, University Of S\~ao Paulo), Louren\c{c}o A. P. J\'unior (aeronautics Institute Of Technology), Leonardo Gon\c{c}alves Chahud (aeronautics Institute Of Technology), J\'ulio Cezar Estrella (university Of S\~ao Paulo), Marcus Botacin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A YARA rule is easy to distribute, but the malware sample used to demonstrate a positive match is not. This complicates storage, continuous integration, disaster-recovery exercises, and reproducible scanner validation. Constructing a replacement fixture requires more than embedding literals: YARA conditions can combine alternatives, counts, offsets, integer reads, and executable-container constraints, while the resulting file should not reproduce malware behavior. Positive validation is existential: it requires one file-level member of a rule's match set, not reconstruction of the originating sample. We present Aray, a deterministic-first YARA interpreter and positive-fixture synthesizer. Models may propose constructive normalizations or typed extraction fallbacks, but never backend source or binary structure. Conventional code validates normalized rules, derives string and integer witnesses, and performs extraction, routing, collision-checked layout, and ELF, PE, or generic serialization. Only residual normalization semantics reach a bounded model judge. We evaluated Aray over 416 public-rule entries. Normalization accepted 182 entries without model assistance and 234 after model normalization. Constructibility preflight admitted 406 entries, and every admitted fixture matched its upstream original rule. This yields 406/416 (97.6%) overall and 406/406 among constructible rules, with ten expected preflight dispositions and no scanner mismatches or construction failures. An unreachable endpoint confirmed zero model invocations during realization. The original-rule oracle validates generated fixtures against their source rules; proving implication for all possible files is a separate, stronger objective. Two anchored-regex failures were repaired before the final run, so these are post-fix systems results, not a held-out estimate.
tldr: Presents Aray, a deterministic-first YARA rule interpreter and artifact synthesizer that generates benign files (ELF/PE) that match YARA rules for validation without reproducing malware behavior.
motivation: YARA rules are easy to distribute, but the malware samples used for positive matching are not, complicating storage, CI, and reproducible scanner validation; constructing replacement fixtures is non-trivial.
method: Aray uses a deterministic-first interpreter that normalizes YARA rules, derives string and integer witnesses, and performs extraction, layout, and serialization to ELF/PE/generic formats, with only residual normalization semantics handled by a bounded model judge.
result: Evaluated on 416 public-rule entries: normalization accepted 182 without model assistance and 234 with model assistance; constructibility preflight admitted 406, and every admitted fixture matched its upstream original rule (406/416 overall, 97.6%).
conclusion: Aray demonstrates feasibility of deterministic artifact synthesis for YARA validation, achieving high success on constructible rules with zero model invocations during realization, though it does not prove implication for all possible files.

title: The Complexity Of Boolean Connectivity Problem Of $k$-Horn Formulas
authors: Takashi Horiyama, Shoon Mineyoshi, Yuto Okura, Kazuhisa Seto, Junichi Teruyama
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Boolean connectivity problem asks whether the set of satisfying assignments of a given Boolean formula forms a connected subgraph in the [MATH]-dimensional hypercube. This problem is known to be [MATH]-complete, even when restricted to [MATH]-Horn formulas for [MATH], as shown by Makino, Tamaki, and Yamamoto. In this paper, we further investigate the computational complexity of {\sc Conn [MATH]-Horn}, the Boolean connectivity problem for [MATH]-Horn formulas. We provide algorithmic and hardness results for {\sc Conn [MATH]-Horn}. On the algorithmic side, we first present an exact exponential-time algorithm for arbitrary [MATH] without any structural restrictions. Our algorithm builds on the deterministic PPZ algorithm proposed by Paturi, Pudl\'{a}k, and Zane. It runs in [MATH] time and polynomial space, achieving an exponential improvement over the previously known algorithm for the Boolean connectivity problem of [MATH]-CNF formulas, shown by Makino, Tamaki, and Yamamoto. We next give two polynomial-time algorithms for arbitrary [MATH] under the following two restrictions: (i) each variable appears at most twice, and (ii) each clause has length exactly [MATH] and each variable appears at most [MATH] times. On the hardness side, we prove that {\sc Conn [MATH]-Horn} remains [MATH]-complete even when each variable appears exactly three times.
tldr: This paper investigates the computational complexity of the Boolean connectivity problem for k-Horn formulas, providing algorithmic and hardness results.
motivation: The Boolean connectivity problem is PSPACE-complete for k-Horn formulas, and the authors aim to improve algorithmic bounds and explore structural restrictions that make the problem tractable.
method: The authors design an exact exponential-time algorithm based on the PPZ algorithm, two polynomial-time algorithms for restricted variable occurrences, and a hardness proof showing PSPACE-completeness even when each variable appears exactly three times.
result: The exponential algorithm achieves an exponential improvement over previous algorithms, and the hardness result tightens the condition for PSPACE-completeness.
conclusion: The paper contributes new complexity results for Boolean connectivity of Horn formulas, but its focus is on classical computational complexity with no connection to quantum information or related directions.

title: Pod-Deployability In Kubernetes With Inter-Pod Affinity Constraints Is PSPACE-Complete
authors: Saverio Giallorenzo, Jacopo Mauro, Gianluigi Zavattaro
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kubernetes is the de-facto platform for container orchestration. Its scheduler combines resource capacities with label-based affinity and anti-affinity rules, and the interaction of these features can make the eventual placement of a pod. In this paper, we study the pod-deployability problem: given an initial cluster, a pod type, and a designated node, does some legal sequence of pod deployments and deletions cover the target pair? We give three complexity results. First, when dynamic constraints contain no affinity (anti-affinity is allowed), pod-deployability is decidable in polynomial time. Second, required affinity together with required anti-affinity makes the problem PSPACE-complete. Third, required affinity alone is already enough for PSPACE-completeness on a single node with one scalar capacity. The lower bounds encode, respectively, 1-safe Petri-net coverability and bounded black pebbling. These results isolate two independent sources of state-space complexity in Kubernetes scheduling: logical exclusion and resource-bounded prerequisite management.
tldr: The paper proves that pod-deployability in Kubernetes with inter-pod affinity constraints is PSPACE-complete.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of Kubernetes scheduling under affinity and anti-affinity rules.
method: Reductions from 1-safe Petri-net coverability and bounded black pebbling to show lower bounds.
result: Pod-deployability is polynomial-time decidable without affinity, but PSPACE-complete with affinity (and even with anti-affinity alone on a single node).
conclusion: The state-space complexity arises from logical exclusion and resource-bounded prerequisites, making general pod-deployability intractable.

title: Securing Filesystems For Confidential Computing
authors: Dimitra Giantsidi, Antoine Delignat-Lavaud, C\'edric Fournet, Jinnan Guo, Heidi Howard, Tianjiao Huang, Kapil Vaswani, Stavros Volos
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidential computing protects applications inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), but it leaves storage vulnerable. Even with disk encryption, a malicious cloud provider can roll back, replay, fork, or tamper with disk state, breaking the integrity and freshness guarantees required by stateful applications. Existing solutions either assume trusted storage, incur high overheads, or push integrity logic into applications. We present ShieldFS, a POSIX-compliant filesystem that provides end-to-end integrity and freshness for persistent storage in the confidential-computing threat model without requiring application changes. ShieldFS represents permissible filesystem states using succinct cryptographic commitments, maintained inside TEEs and replicated in a lightweight trusted registry. On-disk data structures, including a write-ahead log and a storage pool, are authenticated using hash chains and an embedded Merkle tree. ShieldFS utilizes transactions and copy-on-write to update persistent filesystem state and commitments atomically. The commitments are verified during reads, ensuring that rollback, replay, and equivocation attacks are detected even when the entire I/O stack is untrusted. We implement the design by extending ZFS, yielding ShieldZFS. Evaluation with standard filesystem benchmarks and real-world workloads shows that ShieldZFS provides strong integrity and freshness guarantees with performance comparable to state-of-the-art filesystems.
tldr: ShieldFS is a POSIX-compliant filesystem that provides end-to-end integrity and freshness for persistent storage in confidential computing environments without application changes.
motivation: Confidential computing protects applications inside TEEs but leaves storage vulnerable to rollback, replay, fork, or tampering by a malicious cloud provider; existing solutions are insufficient.
method: ShieldFS uses succinct cryptographic commitments maintained inside TEEs, replicated in a trusted registry, and authenticates on-disk data structures with hash chains and an embedded Merkle tree, using transactions and copy-on-write for atomic updates.
result: Evaluation with benchmarks shows ShieldZFS provides strong integrity and freshness guarantees with performance comparable to state-of-the-art filesystems.
conclusion: The paper demonstrates that it is possible to secure filesystems against malicious storage in confidential computing without requiring application modifications, with acceptable performance.

title: From Noise To Signal: Improving Security Log Anomaly Detection Using LLMs With Endpoint-Specific Logs
authors: Gour Karmakar Christopher Henshaw
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing approaches to anomalous behaviour log detection, such as Wazuh rely primarily on predefined detection rules, while statistical anomaly detection approaches such as OpenSearch identify deviations from previously observed behavioural patterns. Recent research has investigated LLMs for log anomaly detection because of their ability to interpret semantic and contextual information. However, LLM-based approaches can be affected by prompt construction, noisy log data, and reliance on generic datasets that may lack endpoint-specific authentication behaviours. To address these limitations, this study develops a standardised instruction-based LLM classification framework for detecting anomalous authentication behaviours, including borderline cases. A controlled cybersecurity testbed was developed to generate endpoint-specific authentication data, producing a curated dataset comprising normal, borderline, and anomalous behavioural scenarios. Three instruction-tuned LLMs, Meta Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, and GPT-OSS 20B, were evaluated against Wazuh rule-based detection and OpenSearch Anomaly Detection using a common ground-truth severity framework. Meta Llama 3.1 8B Instruct achieved the strongest overall end-to-end detection performance, with an accuracy of 89.3%, recall of 88.2%, F1-score of 91.8%, and false negative rate of 11.8%. In comparison, Wazuh achieved an accuracy of 52.0% and false negative rate of 68.6%, while OpenSearch achieved an accuracy of 49.3% and false negative rate of 74.5%. Meta Llama also detected 80% of the borderline anomalous scenarios, compared with 20% for Wazuh and 15% for OpenSearch. Qwen achieved lower overall detection performance than Meta Llama but recorded the lowest average inference latency and 100% structured-response validity. GPT-OSS demonstrated strong classification performance when valid responses were produced.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that instruction-tuned LLMs can outperform traditional anomaly detection systems in detecting authentication log anomalies, particularly for borderline cases.
motivation: Existing rule-based and statistical log anomaly detection methods struggle with borderline cases and lack semantic understanding. LLMs can interpret contextual information but are affected by noise and generic datasets.
method: A standardized instruction-based LLM classification framework was developed, and a controlled cybersecurity testbed generated endpoint-specific authentication data. Three instruction-tuned LLMs (Meta Llama, Qwen, GPT-OSS) were evaluated against Wazuh and OpenSearch using a ground-truth severity framework.
result: Meta Llama achieved the best detection performance with 89.3% accuracy, 88.2% recall, and 91.8% F1-score, detecting 80% of borderline cases compared to 20% for Wazuh and 15% for OpenSearch. Qwen had lower detection but lowest latency, and GPT-OSS performed well when valid responses were produced.
conclusion: LLM-based approaches significantly improve log anomaly detection over traditional methods, especially for nuanced borderline scenarios, at the cost of inference latency.

title: Temporal Fair Division Of Indivisible Mixed Manna: Tractable Settings
authors: Kui-Wang Choi, Minming Li, Nicholas Teh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study temporal fair division of indivisible mixed manna. Items arrive over time and must be allocated irrevocably; an item may be a good for some agents, a chore for others, and neutral for the rest. We require the cumulative allocation after every round to be envy-free up to one item (TEF1). Although deciding whether a TEF1 allocation exists is NP-hard even for goods, we identify several tractable settings. First, with at most [MATH] item types, an online cyclic rule guarantees EF[MATH] after every item arrival. Thus, every instance with at most two types admits an online TEF1 allocation; moreover, when the numbers of agents and types are fixed, TEF1 existence can be decided in polynomial time. Second, under agreement after agent-specific scaling, provided that the scaling factors are known before arrivals begin, an online rule produces an allocation that is EF1 and Pareto optimal after every item arrival. Third, for a two-part arrival sequence with common rankings, we give a rule that is EF1 after every item arrival. Fourth, when the number of agents is fixed and values are bounded integers, we give an exact pseudo-polynomial algorithm for deciding TEF1 existence. Finally, for goods, every TEF1 allocation gives each agent at least [MATH] of her maximin share after every round; this factor is tight even for identical valuations and two rounds. Deciding whether an exact temporal maximin-share allocation exists is NP-hard for both goods and chores, even with identical valuations, two agents, and two rounds.
tldr: This paper studies temporal fair division of indivisible mixed manna (goods, chores, neutral items) with envy-free up to one item (TEF1) requirements, identifying several tractable settings and hardness results.
motivation: Fair division of items arriving over time with irrevocable allocations is challenging, especially when items can be good for some and bad for others. The paper aims to determine when TEF1 allocations exist and can be computed efficiently.
method: The authors propose online cyclic rules for limited item types, an online rule with known scaling factors for Pareto-optimal EF1 allocations, a rule for two-part arrivals with common rankings, and a pseudo-polynomial algorithm for fixed agents and bounded integer values. They also analyze maximin share guarantees and prove NP-hardness for exact temporal maximin-share allocations.
result: They show that TEF1 allocations always exist for at most two item types, and provide polynomial-time algorithms for several other settings. They also establish a tight lower bound on agents' maximin share under TEF1 and prove NP-hardness for exact temporal maximin-share allocation even for identical valuations.
